tokenizer.probe: CoWoS 2.9x $376.1bn remaining performance obligation — Ascend 910C, the ISO's queue.

chunks.heading: agentinf-anthropic-code-exec-free-hours
chunks.text: Anthropic grants each organization 1,550 free container-hours of code execution per month and bills additional usage at 0.05 USD per container-hour, with code execution free of charge entirely when used alongside its web search or web fetch tools, as of July 2026. The bundling clause is the load-bearing part: "Code execution is free when used with web search or web fetch (web_search_20260209 ... or later)" — i.e. free for the most common agent pattern (search, filter, act), because the same sandbox performs dynamic filtering of search results before they reach the context window. A standalone sandbox vendor is pricing against zero for that workload. Compare E2B Pro at $150/mo plus usage.

chunks.heading: agentinf-anthropic-tool-search-token-cut
chunks.text: Anthropic's Tool Search Tool reduced token usage by 85 percent while preserving access to a full tool library, and Programmatic Tool Calling cut average token usage on complex research tasks from 43,588 to 27,297, a 37 percent reduction, in features released 24 November 2025. Company-published benchmarks, not independent. Same post: accuracy on tool selection rose from 49% to 74% (Opus 4) and 79.5% to 88.1% (Opus 4.5); tool-use examples lifted complex-parameter accuracy from 72% to 90%. Read alongside infere-mcp-code-exec-token-cut: within three weeks in November 2025 Anthropic shipped two separate absorptions of tool-routing and tool-registry work that middleware vendors had been selling.

chunks.heading: agentinf-arize-ax-pro-price
chunks.text: Arize AX Pro is priced at 50 USD per month including 50,000 spans, with a free tier of 25,000 spans per month, as of July 2026. No overage rate is published for any tier — a gap worth naming, because in volumetric observability the overage rate is the actual price. Enterprise is the only self-hosted option. Compare Braintrust Pro at $249/mo for 50k scores and Langfuse Core at $29/mo for 100k units: four vendors metering near-identical units within roughly one order of magnitude.

chunks.heading: agentinf-arize-series-c
chunks.text: Arize AI raised a 70 million USD Series C led by Adams Street Partners, announced 20 February 2025, with participation from Microsoft's M12, Datadog and PagerDuty. No valuation, ARR or customer count disclosed. The cap table is the finding: Datadog and PagerDuty — the two incumbent APM vendors most exposed to AI observability — bought an option on the category rather than building it, alongside Microsoft's fund. Phoenix, Arize's open-source tracing library, at 2M+ monthly downloads sets the same open-core price ceiling Langfuse does.

chunks.heading: agentinf-braintrust-series-b-valuation
chunks.text: Braintrust raised an 80 million USD Series B led by ICONIQ Capital at an 800 million USD valuation, announced 17 February 2026, bringing total funding to 121 million USD. The $80M and the investor list are on Braintrust's own blog; the $800M valuation appears only in press coverage, not in the company post — hence medium confidence on the valuation. Named customers: Notion, Replit, Cloudflare, Ramp, Dropbox. NO ARR, customer count or volume metric is disclosed anywhere, so no revenue multiple can be computed — a material gap when the corpus already has LangChain's ~80-100x multiple for comparison. Say so on the page rather than substituting an estimate.

chunks.heading: agentinf-chroma-storage-price
chunks.text: Chroma Cloud charges 0.33 USD per gibibyte per month for storage, 2.50 USD per gibibyte written and 0.0075 USD per tebibyte queried, as of July 2026. Identical headline storage rate to Pinecone Standard ($0.33/GB/mo) — direct evidence of price convergence in the vector layer. Starter $0/mo plus usage with $5 credits; Team $250/mo with $100 credits. Chroma prices queries by data scanned rather than by read unit, which makes cross-vendor comparison hard on purpose.

chunks.heading: agentinf-cloudflare-container-included
chunks.text: Cloudflare includes 25 GiB-hours of container memory, 375 vCPU-minutes and 200 GB-hours of disk per month in the existing Workers Paid plan, charging 0.000020 USD per additional vCPU-second, as of July 2026. Billed in 10ms increments while the container runs; CPU charged on actual use, memory and disk on provisioned size. Instance types from lite (1/16 vCPU, 256 MiB) to standard-4 (4 vCPU, 12 GiB). The competitive mechanism is bundling, not price: agent sandboxing arrives as a line item on a bill the customer already pays, which is the same play the frontier labs are running one layer up.

chunks.heading: agentinf-coreweave-wandb-acquisition
chunks.text: CoreWeave completed its acquisition of Weights & Biases on 5 May 2025 in a transaction reported at 1.7 billion USD, with Weights & Biases reporting approximately 1 million users. The close date is confirmed by CoreWeave's own investor release; the $1.7bn price is REPORTED, not disclosed by either party, and is typed estimate for that reason. The structural point does not depend on the price: the most valuable asset in ML observability did not stay independent, it became a differentiator on a GPU cloud's bill. If the terminal state of observability is 'feature of the compute vendor', that is absorption by layer 4/5 rather than by the model — a different failure mode than the one the layer's bear case usually names.

chunks.heading: agentinf-crewai-no-list-price
chunks.text: CrewAI publishes no list price above a free tier limited to 50 workflow executions per month, quoting its Enterprise plan in 50 hours of development per month rather than in software consumption, as of July 2026. value is null and unit is not_disclosed because CrewAI publishes no number for its paid tier — do not substitute an estimate. The finding is the shape of the offer: for one of the most-starred agent frameworks, the monetized unit at the enterprise tier is services hours, not software. That is the pattern of a framework whose software layer is being absorbed, monetizing the integration labour instead. Contrast Temporal (metered Actions) and Langfuse (metered units).

chunks.heading: agentinf-e2b-series-a
chunks.text: E2B raised a 21 million USD Series A led by Insight Partners, announced 28 July 2025, bringing total venture funding to approximately 32 million USD, with no valuation disclosed. Neither valuation nor revenue is disclosed anywhere reachable — do not substitute an aggregator estimate. Co-investors Decibel, Sunflower Capital, Kaya. Context for the layer: $21M is small relative to the frontier-lab pricing E2B competes against (Anthropic free-with-search; Gemini zero session runtime; Cloudflare bundling 25 GiB-hours into an existing Workers plan).

chunks.heading: agentinf-gemini-file-search-index-price
chunks.text: Google's Gemini File Search tool charges 0.15 USD per million tokens for initial file indexing and charges nothing for storage or for query-time embedding generation, as of its launch on 6 November 2025. Google describes it as "a fully managed RAG system" that removes the need to self-manage a vector database and retrieval pipeline. This is the most aggressive commoditization move in layer 12: the entire managed-retrieval pipeline is priced as a one-time indexing charge, against Pinecone Standard at $0.33/GB/mo plus $16-18 per million read units. Directly undercuts the storage-plus-reads business model shared by Pinecone, Chroma and turbopuffer.

chunks.heading: agentinf-gemini3-grounding-price-cut
chunks.text: Google prices Google Search grounding for Gemini 3 models at 14 USD per 1,000 search queries after 5,000 free prompts per month, against 35 USD per 1,000 grounded prompts for Gemini 2.5 models, as of July 2026. A 60% price cut on grounded search across one model generation, with the free allowance restructured from 1,500/day to 5,000/month. OpenAI's comparable web search tool is $10.00 per 1,000 calls plus search-content tokens. Retrieval-as-a-tool is deflating inside the model API at a rate no standalone retrieval vendor can match on its own cost base.

chunks.heading: agentinf-langfuse-unit-overage
chunks.text: Langfuse Cloud charges 8 USD per 100,000 observability units above plan, graduating down to 6 USD per 100,000 units above 50 million units per month, as of July 2026. Hobby free (50k units), Core $29/mo, Pro $199/mo, Enterprise $2,499/mo — and every paid tier includes the same 100,000 units, so the enterprise premium buys SSO, support and compliance rather than volume. Langfuse is open-source-core: this schedule is the effective ceiling on what closed evals vendors can charge per trace, which is the central weakness in the 'evals are durable' argument.

chunks.heading: agentinf-llamacloud-credit-price
chunks.text: LlamaCloud prices 1,000 credits at 1.25 USD, with plan tiers at 0 USD for 10,000 credits, 50 USD per month for 40,000 credits and 500 USD per month for 400,000 credits, as of July 2026. Enterprise adds volume credit discounts, 5x rate limits, SSO and a named account manager. No revenue, ARR, customer count or funding update is published by LlamaIndex. Credits abstract away the underlying unit (pages parsed, index operations), which prevents direct comparison against Gemini File Search's $0.15/1M indexing tokens — worth flagging as a deliberate opacity pattern across this sub-segment.

chunks.heading: agentinf-mcp-linux-foundation-governance
chunks.text: Anthropic donated the Model Context Protocol to the Agentic AI Foundation, a directed fund under the Linux Foundation co-founded with Block and OpenAI, on 9 December 2025. Sibling founding projects: Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md. AAIF Governing Board holds strategic decisions; MCP retains technical autonomy and its existing maintainer structure. Governance consequence for the layer: owning the connector standard is no longer available as a middleware moat — the spec is now neutral by construction, which removes both a risk and a differentiator.

chunks.heading: agentinf-mcp-servers-sdk-downloads
chunks.text: The Model Context Protocol had more than 10,000 active public servers and more than 97 million monthly SDK downloads across Python and TypeScript as of 9 December 2025. Anthropic's own count, corroborated verbatim on the project blog it controls — one organization, two properties, not independent replication. Third-party registry counts diverge by an order of magnitude (see research/unverified.md, 2026-07-25) and every source for them was an inadmissible aggregator blog. Client support named: ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, VS Code — adoption by direct competitors is the durable part of the datapoint.

chunks.heading: agentinf-modal-sandbox-markup
chunks.text: Modal prices Sandbox CPU at 0.00003942 USD per core-second against 0.0000131 USD per core-second for its standard compute, a 3.0 times internal markup, as of July 2026. Derived: 0.00003942 / 0.0000131 = 3.01. Same for memory: $0.00000667 vs $0.00000222 per GiB/s, also 3.0x. Modal charges a 3x premium for the sandbox wrapper around its own silicon, at the same moment two frontier labs price session runtime at zero. Plan tiers: Starter $0 + compute ($30/mo credits, 100 containers), Team $250 + compute ($100/mo credits, 1,000 containers).

chunks.heading: agentinf-openai-agent-builder-shutdown
chunks.text: OpenAI has announced the deprecation of Agent Builder, its visual agent-orchestration product, with shutdown scheduled for 30 November 2026. Announced October 2025 as part of AgentKit; being retired roughly 13 months later. The single sharpest datapoint in the layer: the frontier lab that shipped a first-party competitor to LangGraph/CrewAI-style visual orchestration is switching it off. No pricing was ever published for it. Both readings belong on the layer page.

chunks.heading: agentinf-openai-code-interpreter-session-price
chunks.text: OpenAI prices code-interpreter containers at 0.03 USD per 20-minute session for 1 GB of memory, rising to 1.92 USD for 64 GB, billed by the minute with a five-minute minimum, as of July 2026. Same page: file search $0.10/GB/day storage (1 GB free) plus $2.50 per 1,000 tool calls; web search $10.00 per 1,000 calls plus search-content tokens. Google prices code execution at standard model token rates with explicitly no charge for session runtime. Three frontier labs, three ways of pricing the sandbox at or near zero.

chunks.heading: agentinf-pinecone-arr-estimate-latka
chunks.text: Latka estimates Pinecone's annual recurring revenue at 26.6 million USD for 2025, unchanged from 2024, against a last-disclosed valuation of 750 million USD. This is LATKA'S MODEL, not a disclosure — Latka is a self-reported/scraped database and is tier 3. Included only because it is the single most-cited number in the vector-commoditization argument and the site is better off naming its provenance than repeating it anonymously. $750M is the April 2023 Series B mark, i.e. a three-year-old price, not a current one. If the layer page uses this at all it must appear with 'Latka estimates' in the sentence. Do not upgrade past low.

chunks.heading: agentinf-pinecone-ceo-transition
chunks.text: Pinecone founder Edo Liberty moved from chief executive to chief scientist on 8 September 2025, with Ash Ashutosh appointed chief executive. In the same interview Ashutosh said acquisition is "definitely not on the table right now" — cite that against any claim that Pinecone is for sale. The competitive set he named is the substantive part: AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle and Databricks, i.e. platforms that added vector search as a feature, plus Milvus and Chroma. He did not name pgvector. Neither ARR nor customer count nor valuation is disclosed in any reachable primary source; see research/unverified.md for what was rejected.

chunks.heading: agentinf-pinecone-standard-read-unit-price
chunks.text: Pinecone's Standard plan carries a 50 USD per month minimum and charges 16 to 18 USD per million read units, 4 to 4.50 USD per million write units and 0.33 USD per gigabyte per month of storage, as of July 2026. Enterprise tier is $500/mo minimum with read units at $24-27 and writes at $6-6.75 per million — a ~50% price uplift for the same units. Builder $20/mo flat. Embedding inference $0.16/M tokens (llama-text-embed-v2). Set this against Gemini File Search: free storage, free query-time embeddings, $0.15/1M tokens to index once. Pinecone's entire meter is what Google now gives away.

chunks.heading: agentinf-temporal-cloud-min-price
chunks.text: Temporal Cloud's Essentials plan carries a 100 USD per month minimum including 1 million Actions, with marginal Actions priced from 50 USD down to 25 USD per million at volume, as of July 2026. Business $500/mo (2.5M Actions), Enterprise contact-sales (10M Actions). Active storage $0.042/GB-hr, retained storage $0.00105/GB-hr. $1,000 in starting credits. Metered on Actions — i.e. on agent step count — so orchestration revenue is a derivative of layer-11 token throughput, the same coupling as evals pricing.

chunks.heading: agentinf-temporal-cloud-ndr
chunks.text: Temporal reported 184 percent net dollar retention, more than 2,500 Temporal Cloud customers and 4.4 times revenue growth over the preceding 18 months, as of 31 March 2025. Company-selected metrics in a funding announcement; no auditor, no definition of the customer or NDR cohort published. Confidence held at medium for that reason. Also disclosed: 183,000+ weekly active open-source developers, 7M+ unique clusters, 600% developer-adoption growth in 18 months. The substantive claim underneath is that durable execution — retries, timers, crash-surviving state — is an operational guarantee no model weight provides. This is the strongest non-absorbable thesis in layer 12 and it is held by a pre-LLM company.

chunks.heading: agentinf-temporal-series-c-valuation
chunks.text: Temporal Technologies raised 146 million USD at a 1.72 billion USD post-money valuation on 31 March 2025, led by Tiger Global, bringing total funding to 350 million USD. Company announcement — a claim, not a filing. Investors: Tiger Global (lead), StepStone, Amplify, Index, MongoDB Ventures, Sequoia, Conversion Capital, 137 Ventures. Compare LangChain at $1.25B on reported $12-16M ARR: Temporal's disclosed operating metrics are far denser, which is itself the point — the orchestration vendor with real retention numbers is the one that predates LLMs.

chunks.heading: agentinf-turbopuffer-tier-minimums
chunks.text: turbopuffer sets monthly usage minimums of 16 USD on Launch, 256 USD on Scale and 4,096 USD on Enterprise, the last carrying a 35 percent usage premium, as of July 2026. Per-unit storage, write and query rates are NOT published on the page — they sit behind a JavaScript cost calculator that did not render, so no per-GB comparison against Pinecone or Chroma is possible from this source. Recorded here as the tier minimum only. The 35% Enterprise usage premium on top of a 16x higher floor is the sharpest published enterprise-uplift in the retrieval sub-segment.

chunks.heading: agentinf-weave-ingest-overage
chunks.text: Weights & Biases charges 0.10 USD per megabyte for Weave observability data ingestion above plan allowances, with the Pro plan starting at 60 USD per month and including 1.5 gigabytes per month, as of July 2026. $0.10/MB is $100/GB — roughly 300x Pinecone's $0.33/GB/mo storage rate, because it prices ingestion of trace payloads rather than storage. Per-megabyte pricing on agent traces is a metered-bandwidth business. Free tier 1 GB/mo Weave ingestion; academic Pro grants 25 GB/mo.

chunks.heading: applic-abridge-arr-2025-05
chunks.text: Abridge reached $100 million ARR in May 2025, up from $60 million at the end of 2024. Contracted ARR $117M in Q1 2025 per same source. 2026 ARR not publicly disclosed — flagged stale. SINGLE-SOURCE (Sacra): apparent corroborators in circulation restate Sacra near-verbatim and do not count. Must not anchor a headline claim or verdict box alone.

chunks.heading: applic-abridge-funding-2026-04
chunks.text: Abridge is reported by secondary-market data providers to have raised a $316 million Series E extension in April 2026. NOT company-confirmed and not covered by quality press. The only non-Sacra source states the figures come from secondary-market data providers, not direct company disclosure. The well-corroborated Abridge round is the June 2025 $300M Series E at $5.3B. Do not use the $316M as a hard funding datapoint. Also unverified: 'Kaiser deployment spans 24,600 physicians; 250+ health systems' — independent 2025 coverage says 100+ health systems, 8K-60K clinicians.

chunks.heading: applic-abridge-seat-price
chunks.text: Abridge enterprise subscriptions are priced at approximately $2,500 per clinician per year. Sacra states 'approximately' (it does not label this an estimate). Bottom-up competitors price at $99-119 per clinician per month (Freed, Nabla); Nuance DAX at ~$600/month. Single-source; comparator prices in notes (Freed/Nabla, Nuance DAX) are also unverified.

chunks.heading: applic-anthropic-1m-customers-2026
chunks.text: More than 1,000 Anthropic customers spend more than $1 million annually as of April 2026. Same sources: 8 of the Fortune 10 are Claude customers; $100K+ accounts grew 7x in a year.

chunks.heading: applic-anthropic-api-mix
chunks.text: Pay-per-token API calls generated approximately 70 to 75 percent of Anthropic revenue as of mid-2026. Value is midpoint of Sacra's 70-75% range; subscriptions 10-15%. CONFLATION HAZARD: never state '80% from API'. Sacra's 70-75% API share is unsourced; the separate ~80% figure Reuters reported is revenue from BUSINESS customers, which is a different cut. The circulating '80% from API' claim looks like a corruption of the Reuters line.

chunks.heading: applic-anthropic-biz-customers-2025-10
chunks.text: Anthropic had more than 300,000 business customers accounting for approximately 80 percent of revenue as of October 2025. PARTIAL corroboration only: the 80%-of-revenue-from-businesses clause is independently corroborated (Reuters, quoting an Anthropic spokesperson); the 300,000+ business-customer count is Sacra-lineage only.

chunks.heading: applic-anthropic-rev-2025
chunks.text: Anthropic revenue run-rate was approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025. STALE: this is the end-2025 historical point. Sacra's own page now reads $47B annualized as of May 2026 (path: $14B Feb -> $19B Mar -> $30B Apr -> $47B May 2026) — see founda-anthropic-runrate-2026-05. Anthropic filed a confidential S-1 on 1 Jun 2026.

chunks.heading: applic-anthropic-runrate-2026-02
chunks.text: Anthropic run-rate revenue was $14 billion on February 12, 2026. Company-disclosed figure in Series G announcement.

chunks.heading: applic-claude-code-arr-2026-02
chunks.text: Claude Code reached $2.5 billion in annualized revenue in February 2026. Up from $1B annualized in November 2025 per same source; enterprise is over half of Claude Code revenue. An $8B-by-May-2026 figure circulates on aggregators only — see unverified.md. SINGLE-SOURCE (Sacra): apparent corroborators in circulation restate Sacra near-verbatim and do not count. Must not anchor a headline claim or verdict box alone.

chunks.heading: applic-clay-arr-2026-05
chunks.text: Clay reached $150 million ARR in May 2026. $108M end-2025, $30M in 2024; $5B valuation via Jan 2026 DST-led tender. Clay's own release (28 Jan 2026) says the tender came 'as Clay surpassed $100M ARR' — consistent with Sacra's $108M end-2025 but no support for $150M in May 2026.

chunks.heading: applic-clay-pricing-2026-03
chunks.text: Clay cut many native enrichment prices by 50 to 90 percent in March 2026 while restructuring to a dual-meter pricing system. Value is upper bound of the 50-90% cut range. Key commoditization datapoint: input-cost deflation passed to customers while ARR grew $108M to $150M over roughly the same period. SPLIT SUPPORT: the dual-meter restructuring (Data Credits vs Actions) is corroborated T1 on Clay's live pricing page; the 50-90% enrichment price cut is Sacra-only. value:90 is the top of a 50-90% range, not a point. Discrepancy: Sacra cites a '$495 Growth tier'; the live page shows Growth from $446/month and no Pro tier. value nulled with value_range 50-90: the field previously recorded 90, the top of the range, as a point value.

chunks.heading: applic-cursor-arr-2025-11
chunks.text: Cursor reached $1 billion annualized revenue in November 2025. Trajectory per cited refs: $100M ARR Jan 2025, $500M Jun 2025, $1B Nov 2025.

chunks.heading: applic-cursor-arr-2026-05
chunks.text: Cursor (Anysphere) reached $3 billion ARR in May 2026. Bloomberg figure cited via Wikipedia reference; Bloomberg article itself paywalled.

chunks.heading: applic-cursor-spacex-2026-06
chunks.text: SpaceX announced an all-stock acquisition of Anysphere valuing it at $60 billion on June 16, 2026. Expected close Q3 2026 per same refs. Largest disclosed exit in the AI applications layer to date.

chunks.heading: applic-decagon-arr-2025-10
chunks.text: Decagon reached $35 million annualized revenue in October 2025. $10M end-2024. Offers per-conversation and per-resolution pricing (charges only when AI resolves without human intervention). The '~128x trailing annualized revenue — richest multiple in the researched set' conclusion rests entirely on this unverified Sacra denominator. Attribute or soften. SINGLE-SOURCE (Sacra): apparent corroborators in circulation restate Sacra near-verbatim and do not count. Must not anchor a headline claim or verdict box alone.

chunks.heading: applic-decagon-valuation-2026-01
chunks.text: Decagon raised a $250 million Series D at a $4.5 billion valuation in January 2026. ~128x trailing annualized revenue ($35M Oct 2025) — richest multiple in the researched set.

chunks.heading: applic-fin-price-per-resolution
chunks.text: Intercom Fin charges $0.99 per outcome, billing only when it resolves an issue end to end or executes a configured procedure. Company's own live pricing page. Qualifications billed at $9.99; 50-outcome monthly minimum. Anchor datapoint for outcome-based pricing in the layer.

chunks.heading: applic-glean-arr-2025-01
chunks.text: Glean ARR was $100 million at fiscal year end January 31, 2025. Initial contracts typically $100K-$500K annually; enterprise deals can exceed $5M (Sacra). Tested and rejected as a dispute: Glean's Dec 2025 'Doubling Revenue in Nine Months' headline back-solves the $100M crossing to ~Mar 2025 and looks contradictory, but the 5 Feb 2025 announcement settles it in the corpus's favour — 'nine months' is loose marketing arithmetic. Do not re-open.

chunks.heading: applic-glean-arr-2026-05
chunks.text: Glean reached $300 million ARR in May 2026. +89% YoY; $208M end-2025; $1M+ contract segment nearly tripled Jan-Dec 2025.

chunks.heading: applic-harvey-arr-2025-08
chunks.text: Harvey reached $100 million ARR in August 2025, three years after founding.

chunks.heading: applic-harvey-arr-2026-05
chunks.text: Harvey reached $300 million ARR in May 2026. $195M end-2025 per same source. Aggregator figures near $190M correspond to Sacra's end-2025 $195M, NOT to $300M — they are not corroboration. No independent source for $300M exists; last well-sourced Harvey ARR is $100M (Aug 2025, CNBC).

chunks.heading: applic-harvey-seat-price
chunks.text: Harvey's base offering starts at about $1,200 per lawyer per month on 12-month commitments. Floor, not a point price — Sacra's wording is 'starts at'. Harvey publishes no pricing. Reported bands run $1,000-1,200 entry, $1,200-1,500 mid-market, $1,500-2,000+ for AmLaw 100, some enterprise seats at $2,500; seat minimums reported at 25-50. Those band sources are vendor-comparison/SEO pages and are inadmissible under the tier rules, so they are noted but not cited. Expansion signal: median seat count doubles within 12 months.

chunks.heading: applic-harvey-users-2026
chunks.text: Harvey served more than 100,000 lawyers across 1,300 organizations in more than 60 countries as of March 2026. Company-disclosed. Sacra's 142,000 lawyers / 1,500 customers (May 2026) is 42% above Harvey's own count from two months earlier and carries no source — not used. A majority of the Am Law 100 are customers (Harvey); Artificial Lawyer had 42% in Aug 2025.

chunks.heading: applic-harvey-valuation-2026-03
chunks.text: Harvey raised at an $11 billion valuation in March 2026. Path: $3B Feb 2025, $5B Jun 2025, $8B (29 Oct 2025, Forbes), $11B Mar 2026. Approximately 37x forward ARR at $300M. Note: the ~37x forward-ARR multiple inherits an unverified denominator (Harvey's $300M ARR is a Sacra estimate) — attribute it wherever used.

chunks.heading: applic-legora-valuation-2026
chunks.text: Legora raised $550 million at a $5.55 billion valuation in a Series D in March 2026. A $50M extension in April 2026 lifted post-money to $5.6B ($600M raised in the Series D) — the corpus previously welded the two events together as '$5.6B with $550M raised'. Preceded by a $150M Series C at $1.8B (Oct 2025). Legal AI is a two-horse capital race: Harvey $11B + Legora $5.6B. TechCrunch reports Legora crossed $100M ARR by April 2026.

chunks.heading: applic-lovable-arr-2026-05
chunks.text: Lovable reached $500 million annualized revenue in May 2026. $100M Jul 2025, $200M Nov 2025, $250M end-2025. ~8M users Feb 2026; $6.6B valuation Dec 2025.

chunks.heading: applic-lovable-headcount-2026-02
chunks.text: Lovable had 146 full-time employees in February 2026. Implies ~$3.4M annualized revenue per employee at the May 2026 $500M run-rate — the layer's strongest opex-leverage datapoint. AUDIT: reclassified estimate (secondary relay of company claim). Metric-mixing caution: revenue-per-employee must use matched dates — TechCrunch's own pair is $400M / 146 = ~$2.77M, not $500M (June) / 146 (February) = ~$3.4M.

chunks.heading: applic-openai-enterprise-mix-2026
chunks.text: Enterprise represented more than 40 percent of OpenAI revenue in 2026. Sacra: 'on track to reach parity with consumer by end of 2026'; API separately 15-20% of total.

chunks.heading: applic-openai-inference-cost-2025
chunks.text: OpenAI inference costs reached $8.4 billion in 2025. Sacra figure; consistent with prior The Information reporting (paywalled, not used). Lineage: the $8.4B figure originates with Ed Zitron's leaked-document reporting; Sacra is plausibly downstream. That is one original plus one relay, not two independent measurements.

chunks.heading: applic-openai-mau-2026-05
chunks.text: ChatGPT exceeded 1 billion monthly active app users as of May 2026. as_of corrected from 2026-05 to 2026-06: Reuters, citing Sensor Tower, puts the 1-billion-MAU crossing in June 2026 — the corpus previously asserted the threshold a month before it was crossed. Third-party estimate of monthly active APP users, not an OpenAI disclosure. The id's -2026-05 suffix is historical; as_of is authoritative.

chunks.heading: applic-openai-paid-business-2026-02
chunks.text: OpenAI had more than 9 million paying business users as of February 2026.

chunks.heading: applic-openai-paid-consumer-2026-02
chunks.text: OpenAI consumer paid subscribers exceeded 50 million as of February 2026.

chunks.heading: applic-openai-rev-2025
chunks.text: OpenAI annualized revenue was $20 billion at the end of 2025. Merged duplicate cloud-openai-arr-2025 (independently logged by cloud agent) on 2026-07-25. NOTE: END-2025 RUN-RATE; capita-openai-revenue-2025 is FY2025 recognized revenue — different metrics, both kept. Attribution correction: this is on the record from OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar (Reuters, Jan 2026), not a Sacra estimate — which is why it stays type:fact. '$20B' is a floor; The Information puts end-2025 at $21.4B. Do not 'correct' this down to the $12.7B/$13.07B figures in circulation — those are FY2025 recognized revenue, a different metric from the exit run-rate.

chunks.heading: applic-openai-wau-2026-05
chunks.text: ChatGPT exceeded 900 million weekly active users across all platforms as of May 2026. as_of corrected from 2026-05 to 2026-02: OpenAI's own report of 27 Feb 2026 announced 900M weekly active users, alongside 50M consumer subscribers and 9M paying business users, 'more than double the 400 million reported in February 2025'. The id's -2026-05 suffix is historical; as_of is authoritative. Value is a floor.

chunks.heading: applic-perplexity-arr-2026-04
chunks.text: Perplexity reached $500 million annualized revenue in April 2026, up about 335 percent year over year. Sacra estimate. The $232M figure on the same page is a separate full-year-2025 metric and is NOT the base of the 335% (232 -> 500 is +115%); the two comparisons must not be welded into one clause. Independent coverage describes growth as ~5x, implying a ~$115M April-2025 base. 100M+ MAU; $20B valuation Sep 2025; $400M Snap distribution deal Nov 2025; 3-year $750M Microsoft partnership Jan 2026.

chunks.heading: applic-replit-arr-2026-04
chunks.text: Replit reached $525 million annualized revenue in April 2026, up from $300 million at the end of 2025. 50M+ users Mar 2026; $9B valuation Mar 2026 Series D ($400M). SINGLE-SOURCE (Sacra): apparent corroborators in circulation restate Sacra near-verbatim and do not count. Must not anchor a headline claim or verdict box alone.

chunks.heading: applic-replit-gm-2025
chunks.text: Replit gross margins fluctuated between positive 36 percent and negative 14 percent during 2025. value set to null deliberately: a single number cannot represent a range that crosses zero, and value:36 handed any consumer the flattering end. Range is +36% to -14%. Sacra-only — no independent source for Replit gross margin at any date exists (Replit is private and discloses none). Sacra: 'driven by the cost of accessing large language models for its coding agents.' Carries heavy narrative weight as the clearest public evidence that agentic app-layer gross margins can invert, on one unsourced sentence — attribute it wherever used. Replit responded with effort-based agent pricing ($0.06 to multiple dollars per run, replacing flat $0.25 checkpoints).

chunks.heading: applic-sierra-arr-2024-12
chunks.text: Sierra ARR was $26 million at the end of 2024. Implies ~8x growth in 17 months to May 2026. SINGLE-SOURCE (Sacra): apparent corroborators in circulation restate Sacra near-verbatim and do not count. Must not anchor a headline claim or verdict box alone.

chunks.heading: applic-sierra-arr-2026-05
chunks.text: Sierra reached $200 million ARR in May 2026. ~$130M end-2025, $100M crossed Nov 2025. Works with 40% of the Fortune 50; claims 70% containment rates (company claim, uncorroborated). If the site quotes Sierra's valuation multiple, note it is ~79x on Sacra's $200M but ~105x on the company-disclosed >$150M — commit to one denominator.

chunks.heading: applic-sierra-arr-company-2026-02
chunks.text: Sierra stated it had passed $150 million in annual recurring revenue in February 2026, and coverage of its May 2026 round still reported ARR above $150 million. Split out 2026-07-25 so the page is not forced onto the more flattering denominator. Sacra estimates $200M for May 2026 (applic-sierra-arr-2026-05); the company's own figure is '>$150M'. On the $15.8bn valuation that is ~105x rather than ~79x. A site whose whole claim is citation discipline should not quietly pick the estimate that makes the multiple look better — cite both and say which one the text uses.

chunks.heading: applic-sierra-valuation-2026-05
chunks.text: Sierra raised a $950 million Series E at a $15.8 billion post-money valuation in May 2026. ~79x ARR at $200M — among the richest multiples in the layer.

chunks.heading: capita-amd-openai-gw-2025-10
chunks.text: OpenAI agreed in October 2025 to deploy 6 GW of AMD GPUs over five years. First 1 GW of MI450 targeted H2 2026.

chunks.heading: capita-amd-openai-warrant-2025-10
chunks.text: AMD issued OpenAI a warrant on October 5 2025 for up to 160 million AMD shares at $0.01 per share, vesting in tranches tied to Instinct deployments and share-price targets escalating to $600 per share for the final tranche. SOURCE RECOVERED 2026-07-25: the recorded URL was an EDGAR browse-edgar filing-LIST query that 403s and contains no warrant terms. The 8-K confirms every recorded number and adds two: the first tranche vests after the initial 1 GW of MI450, and FULL vesting is contingent on 6 GW — the more load-bearing term than the share count. Warrant expires 2030-10-05; OpenAI gave a concurrent binding commitment to purchase the initial 1 GW. THE 'ABOUT 10 PERCENT OF THE COMPANY' CLAUSE HAS BEEN DROPPED — that figure appears nowhere in the filing; it is press arithmetic on share count.

chunks.heading: capita-anthropic-azure-commit-2025-11
chunks.text: Anthropic committed in November 2025 to purchase 30 billion USD of Azure compute capacity running on NVIDIA systems. Initially up to ~1 GW of capacity.

chunks.heading: capita-anthropic-google-tpu-2025-10
chunks.text: Anthropic and Google signed an October 2025 cloud partnership giving Anthropic access to up to 1 million TPUs and more than 1 GW of capacity by 2026. Confirmed 2025-10-23: up to one million TPUs and more than a gigawatt of capacity by 2026; value 'tens of billions', not disclosed. Source was the bare vktr.com domain, harvested via Wikipedia references. Per CLAUDE.md the Google Cloud press release cannot itself be the fact source.

chunks.heading: capita-apollo-zelter-8tn-estimate-2026-08
chunks.text: Apollo president Jim Zelter said on an August 2026 earnings call that more than $8 trillion of capital is expected to be invested in the AI infrastructure build-out. An estimate from an executive whose firm earns fees financing the build-out. An interested party's claim about intent, not a measurement.

chunks.heading: capita-avgo-purchase-commitments-128bn-2026-08
chunks.text: Broadcom's filings disclose $128 billion of purchase commitments, with $55.2 billion of deliveries scheduled for fiscal 2027 and $72.9 billion for fiscal 2028, relating almost entirely to its agreed purchase of 3.5 GW of TPU hardware from Google. Filing-disclosed, so the firmest number in this structure. The attribution to the TPU purchase is sourced to people familiar.

chunks.heading: capita-aws-openai-2025-11
chunks.text: AWS and OpenAI announced a multi-year compute agreement valued at 38 billion USD in November 2025. ~7 years; hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GB200/GB300 GPUs. Needs URL confirmation at fact-check gate.

chunks.heading: capita-bis-m7-concentration
chunks.text: The Magnificent 7 grew from about 20 percent to nearly 35 percent of S&P 500 market capitalization between November 2022 and late 2025. Same chapter: tech data-center bond issuance met with widening spreads; private credit deal-making cooled.

chunks.heading: capita-bridgewater-capex-2026
chunks.text: Meta, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft were expected to invest about 650 billion USD combined in AI-related infrastructure in 2026, per Bridgewater Associates analysis. Attributed to co-CIO Greg Jensen in a client letter: ~$650B across Alphabet/Amazon/Meta/Microsoft in 2026, UP FROM $410 BILLION IN 2025 — that base independently refutes the $388B the corpus previously carried in cloud-big4-capex-2025-actual. Per-company: Amazon ~$200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Microsoft ~$145B annualized run rate. Bridgewater frames the boom as entering a 'more dangerous phase'. Source was en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta_Platforms with an empty quote_ref.

chunks.heading: capita-burry-depreciation-claim
chunks.text: Michael Burry claimed in November 2025 that hyperscalers would understate depreciation by about 176 billion USD across 2026-2028 by extending server useful lives. Opinion of a named short-seller with positions; steelman both directions. Merged duplicate cloud-burry-depreciation-claim (independently logged by cloud agent) on 2026-07-25.

chunks.heading: capita-compute-spv-35bn-1gw-2026-06
chunks.text: A special-purpose vehicle known as Compute SPV paid $35 billion in June 2026 for roughly 1 GW of TPU hardware, about 1 million chips, funded by three tranches of debt anchored by Apollo and Blackstone and leased on to Anthropic. Arranged by Morgan Stanley as an adaptation of the vendor-financing model Boeing and GE used for aircraft and engines. Sourced to people familiar with the matter.

chunks.heading: capita-coreweave-ddtl-2026-03
chunks.text: CoreWeave closed an $8.5 billion delayed-draw term loan on March 30 2026 through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary, secured by substantially all of that subsidiary's assets and a pledge of its equity, to fund GPU capital expenditure for an unnamed customer contract. THREE CORRECTIONS 2026-07-25, the third material. (a) The facility closed 2026-03-30; February was reporting of talks, and the fact said 'sought'. (b) The 8-K NEVER MENTIONS META. (c) The previous note said the collateral shift was 'from GPUs to customer contracts — lending against counterparty credit rather than asset value'; the filed structure is the OPPOSITE. Security is substantially all assets of CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. VIII, LLC and its subsidiaries plus a 100% equity pledge — the GPUs ARE the lien. The customer contract appears as a covenant and an event-of-default trigger, not as collateral. Terms: 'DDTL 4.0', MUFG administrative agent, MUFG and Morgan Stanley Asset Funding coordinating lead arrangers, commitments available to June 2027, maturity 2032-03-31, SOFR+225bp, 50bp undrawn fee, 1.15x debt-service-coverage covenant, parent guarantee limited to specified bad acts. A 'Meta contracts' framing needs its own attributed Bloomberg citation and must be labelled reporting, not filing. ID RENAMED 2026-07-25 from capita-coreweave-meta-collateral-2026-02: the id itself asserted both Meta and February, neither of which the 8-K supports. An id is not neutral metadata — an author scanning the corpus reads it as a summary, which is how the wrong framing survived the first correction pass.

chunks.heading: capita-coreweave-ddtl-terms-2026-03
chunks.text: CoreWeave's March 2026 delayed-draw term loan priced at SOFR plus 225 basis points with a 50 basis point undrawn fee, a 1.15 times debt-service-coverage covenant and a maturity of 31 March 2032. Split out 2026-07-25 from the notes of capita-coreweave-ddtl-2026-03, where it blocked a whole paragraph. This is the best 'price of AI money' evidence in the corpus: an actual spread, an actual covenant and an actual maturity on an $8.5bn facility, from the filing. MUFG administrative agent; MUFG and Morgan Stanley Asset Funding coordinating lead arrangers; commitments available to June 2027; parent guarantee limited to specified bad acts.

chunks.heading: capita-coreweave-ddtl2-2024
chunks.text: CoreWeave closed a 7.5 billion USD delayed-draw term loan facility in May 2024 led by Blackstone with Magnetar. Interest-rate terms in unverified.md pending S-1 access.

chunks.heading: capita-coreweave-gpu-loan-2023
chunks.text: CoreWeave secured a 2.3 billion USD debt facility led by Magnetar Capital and Blackstone in August 2023, collateralized by NVIDIA H100 GPUs. First at-scale GPU-collateralized loan.

chunks.heading: capita-coreweave-janestreet
chunks.text: Jane Street signed a 6 billion USD AI cloud agreement with CoreWeave and made a 1 billion USD equity investment. Non-hyperscaler, non-lab buyer of GW-scale AI compute — new demand category.

chunks.heading: capita-coreweave-meta-21b
chunks.text: CoreWeave and Meta announced an expanded AI infrastructure agreement of 21 billion USD. Expansion of the initial ~$14.2B September 2025 deal; as_of = observation date, announcement date needs capture. Merged duplicate cloud-crwv-meta-contract (independently logged by cloud agent) on 2026-07-25.

chunks.heading: capita-coreweave-openai-initial
chunks.text: CoreWeave and OpenAI signed an infrastructure agreement of up to 11.9 billion USD in March 2025. OpenAI also took $350M of CoreWeave stock (same PR). Merged duplicate cloud-crwv-openai-contract (independently logged by cloud agent) on 2026-07-25.

chunks.heading: capita-coreweave-openai-total
chunks.text: CoreWeave's combined contracts with OpenAI reached approximately 22.4 billion USD after a further expansion of up to 6.5 billion USD in September 2025. 11.9 + 4.0 (May 2025) + 6.5 = 22.4.

chunks.heading: capita-fed-fsr-ai-salient-risk
chunks.text: 30 percent of Federal Reserve market-outreach contacts cited artificial intelligence among salient financial stability risks in Fall 2025, up from 9 percent in Spring 2025. Report also flags 'a sharp decline in asset prices, potentially connected to a turn in AI sentiment'; data as of 2025-10-23.

chunks.heading: capita-fed-fsr-debt-gdp
chunks.text: Total US private nonfinancial credit outstanding was 42,235 billion USD in Q2 2025, with the debt-to-GDP ratio at its lowest level in two decades. Core steelman datum: AI debt is being layered onto an under-levered corporate sector.

chunks.heading: capita-fluidstack-valuation-18bn-2026-04
chunks.text: Fluidstack was reported in April 2026 to be seeking approximately $1 billion at a valuation of about $18 billion, in a round reported to be led by Jane Street and Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness fund, after an earlier round reported at roughly $7 billion. Low confidence and typed as an estimate on purpose. Fluidstack is private, the reporting describes talks rather than a closed round, and no filing or company document in this corpus confirms any of it. Carried because the counterparty's own capitalisation matters to the leases it has signed, not because the number is solid.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-affiliates-rule-scope-companies
chunks.text: CSIS estimates the September 2025 Entity List affiliates rule added controls on about 20,000 companies in China before its suspension. Interim final rule 'Expansion of End-User Controls To Cover Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities', 90 FR 47201, 2025-09-30, captured any entity at least 50 percent owned by a listed party.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-affiliates-rule-suspension-expiry-2026-11
chunks.text: BIS suspended the Entity List 50-percent affiliates rule for 12 months, with the suspension set to end 9 November 2026 absent an extension. CSIS estimates the suspended rule's scope at about 20,000 companies in China. Expires within days of China's rare-earth suspension (about 10 November 2026). SHARPER AND VERIFIED: the affiliates rule is REIMPOSED effective 10 November 2026 (90 FR 50857: 'This final rule adds back into the EAR effective November 10, 2026') — the SAME DATE ASML records for the rare-earth suspension expiry, not 'within days' as the notes said. Same day is a stronger fact than the one recorded.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-ai-diffusion-rescission-no-replacement-2026-05
chunks.text: NVIDIA reported in May 2026 that the scope, timing and requirements of the rule replacing the rescinded AI Diffusion interim final rule remained uncertain, 12 months after the rescission was announced. A Federal Register API search of BIS documents for 'artificial intelligence diffusion' from 2025-01-01 returns no rescission rule and no replacement. The original IFR (90 FR 4544, 2025-01-15) was the first US control on AI model weights.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-amat-bis-settlement-253m-2026-02
chunks.text: Applied Materials agreed on 11 February 2026 to pay the Bureau of Industry and Security 253 million USD to resolve an inquiry into certain China customer shipments and export controls compliance. Booked as a 'Legal settlement' line in operating expenses for the quarter ended 2026-01-25. DOJ and SEC closed their parallel inquiries with no enforcement action. The settlement carries a suspended denial order; breach would bar AMAT from exporting certain products from the US. Largest disclosed corporate penalty in this domain. FALSE SUPERLATIVE CORRECTED 2026-07-25: the notes claimed 'largest disclosed corporate penalty in this domain'. It is the SECOND-largest, behind Seagate's $300 million (19 April 2023, Huawei foreign-direct-product-rule violations, 7.4 million drives over 429 transactions worth ~$1.1bn), which BIS called the largest standalone administrative penalty in its history and which also carried a five-year suspended denial order — so AMAT's suspended denial order is not novel either. The $253M is verified verbatim in AMAT's 10-Q.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-asml-china-revenue-share-2025
chunks.text: Customers in China represented 29.1 percent of ASML total net sales in 2025, down from 36.1 percent in 2024. ASML 2025 total net sales 32.667 billion EUR (2024: 28.263 billion EUR), up 15.6 percent. Lithography systems sold 327 units (2024: 418); EUV systems recognised 48 (2024: 44). ASML notes its DUV business in China was stronger than anticipated in 2025.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-asml-euv-annual-capacity-2026
chunks.text: ASML stated in July 2026 that its 2026 low-NA EUV capacity is around 65 systems per year, with a plan to add 30 percent for 2027. DUV immersion capacity around 130 systems in 2026, likewise plus 30 percent planned for 2027, with a further 30 percent under investigation for 2028. ASML Q2 2026: 9.3 billion EUR net sales, 2.9 billion EUR net income; FY2026 guidance 43-45 billion EUR at 54-56 percent gross margin. Sixty-five EUV machines a year is the true width of the pipe at the top of the AI stack. DOUBLE-COUNT WARNING 2026-07-25: this and fab-asml-euv-units-2026 are THE SAME NUMBER from the same company on the same day — the press release says 'our 2026 low NA EUV capacity of around 65' (CEO) and the transcript says 'we now expect to ship around 65 Low NA EUV systems this year' (CFO Dassen). Both wordings are source-faithful, but the two facts were typed differently (fact vs forecast) and ANY VIZ USING BOTH DOUBLE-COUNTS. Use one. The 'true width of the pipe' framing also conflates annual flow with installed stock.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-bis-budget-headcount-2024
chunks.text: Gregory C. Allen reported in October 2024 that the Bureau of Industry and Security operated on a budget just under 200 million USD with fewer than 600 employees. Scale contrast: a single alleged diversion scheme moved 2.5 billion USD of servers. Allen also identified at least eight Chinese AI chip-smuggling networks, each with transactions valued above 100 million USD. Figures are 2024-dated; no newer public equivalent found in free sources.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-bis-china-volume-cap-2026-01
chunks.text: The BIS rule effective 15 January 2026 caps licensed China and Macau exports at 50 percent of the aggregate total processing performance cumulatively shipped to United States end users for the same commodity. One of five conditions; others are US supply sufficiency, no foundry diversion, KYC on remote access, and third-party lab testing of every shipment before export. The preamble states this condition loosely in product-volume terms; §(dd)(1)(iii) binds on AGGREGATE TPP, measured cumulatively from when the commodity first shipped to commercial US customers through to the licence-application date. Materially stricter and materially different: a vendor cannot backload China volume, and the ratio is scored against lifetime US TPP. ANY VIZ SHOWING THIS AS A UNIT RATIO MUST BE RELABELLED.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-bis-dram-bandwidth-threshold-2026-01
chunks.text: The BIS rule effective 15 January 2026 caps licensable China and Macau advanced computing exports at total DRAM bandwidth below 6,500 GB/s. Memory bandwidth, not FLOPS, is the operative second gate - it is what separates H200-class from Blackwell-class parts.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-bis-presumption-denial-above-threshold-2026-01
chunks.text: The January 2026 BIS rule imposes nine certification conditions for case-by-case China and Macau licensing and retains a presumption of denial for everything above its thresholds. Verbatim: 'All other applications ... will be reviewed under a presumption of denial to or within Macau or destinations specified in Country Group D:5'. The loosening covers a sub-frontier tier only. The nine conditions: (i) US unit volumes and performance specs; (ii) US supply sufficiency and no foundry diversion; (iii) the 50%-of-aggregate-TPP cap; (iv) no military, military-intelligence or WMD end use or end user; (v) consignee KYC against remote access; (vi) list of IaaS remote end users in Belarus, China, Cuba, Iran, Macau, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela; (vii) IaaS operator will not transfer model weights or grant remote access to restricted parties; (viii) physical-security demonstration; (ix) third-party lab review of every shipment pre-export. The prior count of five came from merging two preamble bullets and dropping the end-use, remote-end-user-list, model-weights and physical-security conditions.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-bis-tpp-threshold-2026-01
chunks.text: Under the BIS rule effective 15 January 2026, advanced computing commodities may be licensed to China and Macau on case-by-case review only if certified below 21,000 total processing performance. Companion threshold in the same condition: total DRAM bandwidth below 6,500 GB/s. Rule names the NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI325X as the reference class. Applies to ECCN 3A090.a and 3A090.b.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-china-chip-localisation-vs-target-2025
chunks.text: Domestically produced chips accounted for about 30 percent of Chinese chip consumption in 2025, against a policy target of 70 percent localisation by end-2025. The clearest single measure of the gap between Chinese industrial-policy ambition and outcome: massive over-delivery on tools and mature nodes, large under-delivery on the headline localisation target.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-china-domestic-ai-chip-share-2026
chunks.text: TrendForce projects the domestic share of China's AI chip market rises to 50 percent in 2026. Relayed by CSIS (Shivakumar, Wessner, Howell). Driven as much by Beijing's November 2025 ban on foreign AI chips in state-funded datacentres as by domestic supply. The 50%-domestic-share projection is TrendForce's, relayed by CSIS — the source org should credit TrendForce, not CSIS, with the number.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-china-equipment-localisation-2025
chunks.text: Chinese-made semiconductor manufacturing equipment rose from 25 percent to 35 percent of China's domestic market between 2024 and 2025, from a pre-controls base of 10 to 15 percent. In etch and thin-film deposition local firms now supply 40 percent of the domestic market. Naura reportedly supplies 60 percent of oxidation and diffusion furnaces for SMIC's 28nm production. Chinese mature-node capacity grew four times faster than global demand 2014-2025 and now accounts for about half of global capacity.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-china-foreign-chip-ban-state-datacentres-2025-11
chunks.text: Chinese guidance issued in November 2025 requires state-funded data centre projects to use only domestically made AI chips, with projects less than 30 percent complete ordered to remove installed foreign chips. Projects further along decided case-by-case. Chinese AI datacentre projects have drawn over 100 billion USD in state funding since 2021. NVIDIA, AMD and Intel are the excluded parties. This, not US policy, is the proximate cause of NVIDIA's zero China datacentre revenue. A country that believed it was choked would not ban the chips it can still get. NVIDIA's 10-Q removed from corroborated_by 2026-07-25: it does not describe this November 2025 ban or the 30%-completion rule. Its adjacent filed language — 'The Chinese government has encouraged customers to purchase from our China-based competitors' and an Action Plan endorsing compute-per-watt and per-memory-bandwidth standards for new and renovated data centers — is circumstantial support only. The <30%-complete threshold is in notes. Two readings differ: Reuters (two anonymous sources, via Business Standard) has projects ordered to REMOVE installed chips plus >$100bn of state funding since 2021; FDD (Burnham/Lazarow, 2025-11-10) independently confirms the threshold but reads the rule as a ban on ACQUIRING foreign chips.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-china-hbm-stockpile
chunks.text: SemiAnalysis estimated China procured 13 million HBM stacks, enough for 1.6 million Ascend 910C packages, with Samsung supplying 11.4 million including 7 million in December 2024. Pre-restriction purchases. SemiAnalysis's framing: 'HBM is The Bottleneck'. Once the stockpile is consumed, Ascend output falls to what domestic HBM can package. 'Including 7 million in December 2024' is an interpretation; SemiAnalysis says the 7M stacks came 'in the 1-month gap between controls announcement and enforcement dates'. Use the source's wording.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-china-rare-earth-suspension-expiry
chunks.text: ASML records that China suspended its rare-earth export restrictions for 12 months until 10 November 2026 as part of a trade agreement with the United States. ASML adds that existing risk-mitigation measures remain in place. The April 2025 licensing regime was never suspended. The two dates may describe distinct measures - keep both. Converges with the US affiliates-rule suspension expiry of 9 November 2026: both truces lapse in the same week. UPGRADED from 'may describe distinct measures' to DO: Tom's Hardware (Luke James, 2025-11-10) is explicit that 27 November 2026 belongs to the gallium, germanium and antimony export ban to the US (lifted effective 9 November 2025), while ASML's 10 November 2026 belongs to the October-2025 rare-earth export restrictions. Two different measures, not a date conflict.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-china-subsidised-dc-utilisation
chunks.text: Data centre utilisation in China's subsidised western AI hubs was just 20 to 30 percent, in regions offering cloud providers power-bill cuts of up to 50 percent. Value is the midpoint of the reported 20-30 percent range. Gansu, Guizhou and Inner Mongolia offer the discounts, conditioned on domestically made chips. The mirror image of the US problem: China gives away power and cannot fill racks; the US has power and cannot get permits. NO COUNTING METHOD EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE CHAIN — USCC footnote -> Light Reading -> an unnamed 'Report'. No definition of utilisation (rack space? power draw? GPU-hours?), no sample, no facility count. The USCC paper carries it as a caveat, not a finding. This matters because the fact was carrying a headline framing ('the mirror image of the US problem') that a methodologically undefined number cannot support.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-china-us-model-lag-months
chunks.text: Epoch AI measured Chinese AI models as trailing leading US releases by 7 months on average since 2023, with a range of 4 to 14 months. Metric is the Epoch Capabilities Index. Every model at the AI capability frontier since 2023 has been US-developed; as of 2026-01-02 no Chinese model had surpassed OpenAI's o3 (April 2025). Most leading Chinese models are open-weight while US frontier models are closed.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-cowos-capacity-end-2026
chunks.text: TSMC CoWoS advanced packaging capacity is reported to reach 120,000 to 140,000 wafers per month by end-2026, with the supply-demand gap narrowing from about 20 percent to about 10 percent. Value is the midpoint of the reported 120,000-140,000 range. Figures attributed by TrendForce to Taiwan's Economic Daily News, not to TSMC, which discloses no CoWoS capacity. OSAT partners add 50,000-60,000 wafers per month for an industry total approaching 200,000. Reuters-sourced CoWoS CAGR above 80 percent from 2022 to 2027. A gap still at 10 percent after 52-56 billion USD of capex means packaging stays rationed through the forecast period. PROVENANCE UNDERSTATED: TrendForce attributes these figures to 'institutional investors' as reported by Taiwan's Economic Daily News — unnamed and third-hand, not to EDN itself as the notes said. The article also says capacity 'could reach a record 120,000 to 140,000 wafers IN 2026', not 'by end-2026'. TSMC discloses no CoWoS capacity. The Reuters-sourced >80% 2022-27 CoWoS CAGR in the notes traces to a TSMC Taiwan Technology Symposium presentation (May 2026) and is the sturdier number.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-deepseek-v32-no-disclosed-training-cost
chunks.text: DeepSeek's V3.2 paper discloses no absolute training compute, GPU count or dollar training cost, reporting only the DeepSeek Sparse Attention mechanism, a reinforcement-learning recipe and an agentic-synthesis pipeline. Submitted 2025-12-02 by DeepSeek-AI with 264 or more listed authors. Widely repeated DeepSeek training-cost figures are not sourced to this paper - I fetched the abstract and confirmed the absence. DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale (December 2025) was, per USCC, the first open model capable of IMO gold-level scores. The absence claim HOLDS, and now against the full PDF rather than the abstract. Two partial disclosures the previous claim overstated as total silence: post-training budget 'exceeds 10% of the pre-training cost' (a ratio), and inference economics benchmarked 'on H800 GPUs, at a rental price of 2 USD per GPU hour'. The string '685' appears nowhere in the paper and no MoE-backbone spec is given for V3.2; MoE appears only in a routing discussion and a DeepSeek-V2 citation. Author count verified: DeepSeek-AI plus 263 co-authors.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-doj-gatekeeper-160m-2025-12
chunks.text: US prosecutors stated that a Texas-based network exported or attempted to export at least 160 million USD of controlled NVIDIA H100 and H200 GPUs between October 2024 and May 2025. Alan Hao Hsu and Hao Global LLC pleaded guilty on 10 October 2025 - a conviction, not an allegation. The US seized over 50 million USD in NVIDIA technologies and cash; Hsu received over 50 million USD in wire transfers originating from the PRC. Announced as Operation Gatekeeper.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-doj-janford-transshipment-2025-11
chunks.text: A November 2025 US indictment charges four defendants with exporting NVIDIA GPUs to China through Malaysia and Thailand from September 2023 to November 2025 using a Florida realty company as a front. Janford Realtor, LLC 'was never involved in any real estate transactions'. Establishes Malaysia and Thailand as the named transshipment corridor. Allegations.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-doj-smci-510m-three-weeks-2025
chunks.text: The same indictment alleges at least approximately 510 million USD of US-assembled servers were diverted to China between late April 2025 and mid-May 2025 alone. Roughly three weeks. Concealment included staging 'thousands of dummy servers' - non-working physical replicas - to defeat the manufacturer's own compliance audits, including an August 2025 audit. Strongest available evidence that OEM end-use verification fails at scale.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-doj-smci-diversion-2500m-2026-03
chunks.text: A March 2026 US indictment alleges that a Southeast Asian intermediary purchased approximately 2.5 billion USD of servers from a US manufacturer between 2024 and 2025 for unlicensed diversion to China. Defendants Yih-Shyan Liaw (co-founder, board member and SVP Business Development of the publicly traded US manufacturer), Ruei-Tsang Chang (GM, Taiwan office, fugitive) and Ting-Wei Sun (broker). Unsealed in SDNY. All figures are allegations, not adjudicated facts.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-entity-list-addition-cadence-2018-2024
chunks.text: Between 2018 and 2024 BIS added entities to the Entity List every 35 days on average. Baseline for the current freeze.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-entity-list-freeze-months-2026-06
chunks.text: As of 26 June 2026, eight months had passed with no additions to the BIS Entity List, the longest such gap since 2008. Last addition October 2025. Koren and Spicher: 'a list that stops expanding tracks fewer of the relevant actors, eroding its value as a control.' They also report that all but one of the seven 2026 export enforcement actions stem from Entity List violations.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-eu-investai-gigafactory-commitment
chunks.text: The European Commission has announced that 20 billion EUR will be mobilised for AI gigafactories through the InvestAI Facility, with the formal tender due summer 2026 and first construction in 2027. Announced 2025-02-09. An informal call produced 77 proposals from 16 Member States across 60 sites (June 2025). EU-EIB MoU 2025-10-22; EuroHPC JU Regulation adapted 2026-01-16, in force 2026-01-20. As of mid-2026, eighteen months after announcement, zero gigafactories are under construction and the tender has not been issued. The 200 billion EUR figure widely quoted is an EU-wide mobilisation target and does not appear on the Commission's gigafactory page. Eighteen months after the 2025-02-09 announcement the tender has not issued, no site is funded and nothing is under construction — which is why 'committed' was the wrong verb. The verification that the EUR 200bn figure is ABSENT from the Commission's gigafactory page is correct and worth keeping.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-gain-ai-act-senate-vote-2025-10
chunks.text: The Senate passed its FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, which included the GAIN AI Act, on 9 October 2025, and the provision was stripped before the Act was signed on 18 December 2025. NVIDIA's 10-Q describes the Act as restricting the administration's ability to adapt export control rules and allowing private US persons to review and overturn licensing decisions. Outcome: export control authority over AI chips remains discretionary and unlegislated. Vote tally and stripping are from secondary sources; NVDA 10-Q confirms Senate passage in the NDAA. The 77-20 tally was the Senate's vote on the FY2026 NDAA (S.2296) AS A WHOLE, with the GAIN AI Act (S.Amdt.3505) inside it — not a vote on the GAIN AI Act, and it appeared in NONE of the three originally cited sources (NVIDIA's 10-Q says only that the Senate passed it within the NDAA). The House version (H.R.3838, 2025-09-10) excluded it. The 18 December 2025 signing and the stripping still need Congress.gov public-law text as a hard source.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-huawei-ascend-developers-2025
chunks.text: Huawei reported more than 4 million Ascend developers and more than 3.8 million Kunpeng developers at end-2025, with the 384-NPU SuperPoD deployed at scale. Company-reported ecosystem metric with no published methodology - log as a claim. The CloudMatrix 384-NPU SuperPoD deployment claim is Huawei's own.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-huawei-ascend-roadmap-2026
chunks.text: Huawei announced at Huawei Connect on 18 September 2025 that the Ascend 950PR ships in Q1 2026 and the 950DT in Q4 2026 with self-developed HBM, against an 800 TFLOPS FP16 and 3.2 TB/s baseline for the 910C. Company roadmap presented by Deputy Chairman Eric Xu - a plan, not shipped product. Also announced: Ascend 960 Q4 2027, 970 Q4 2028; interconnect bandwidth 2.5x prior generation; Atlas 950 SuperPoD 8,192 NPUs (Q4 2025), Atlas 960 SuperPoD 15,488 NPUs (Q4 2027); SuperClusters above 500,000 and above 1,000,000 NPUs. The 910C baseline is described as roughly 80 percent of an NVIDIA H100. 'Presented by Deputy Chairman Eric Xu' is not in the cited TrendForce article — source it or drop the attribution.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-huawei-ascend-units-2025
chunks.text: SemiAnalysis estimated Huawei Ascend shipments of 805,000 units in 2025, of which 653,000 were 910C, up from 507,000 units in 2024. Named analysts, free portion of the article. Reuters reporting (September 2025, unnamed sources) put Huawei's 2026 plan at about 600,000 Ascend 910C chips and up to 1.6 million total Ascend dies. SPREAD DISCLOSED 2026-07-25 — this was a single-source figure on a politically contested number. Independent estimates of 2025 Ascend TOTAL shipments cluster at 700k-805k (SemiAnalysis 805k Sep-2025; Mizuho 700k+ May-2025; Bernstein ~700k). THE 910C SPLIT IS THE CONTESTED PART and the 653k sub-figure is the outlier: SemiAnalysis 653k vs Bernstein ~350k vs Huawei's own early-2025 plan of 100k — roughly 2x and 6.5x respectively. Part of the gap is timing (SemiAnalysis is four months later). Do not present 653k as settled; consider splitting it into its own low-confidence estimate so the total and the split are not co-signed.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-huawei-revenue-2025
chunks.text: Huawei reported 2025 revenue of CNY 880.941 billion (126.018 billion USD) and net profit of CNY 68.036 billion, with R&D of CNY 192.3 billion or 21.8 percent of revenue. Segments: ICT Infrastructure CNY 375.014bn (+2.6 percent), Consumer CNY 344.473bn (+1.6), Digital Power CNY 77.312bn (+12.7), Intelligent Automotive CNY 45.018bn (+72.1), Cloud Computing CNY 32.161bn (MINUS 3.5 percent). Huawei's cloud revenue FELL in the year Chinese AI demand supposedly exploded - Ascend silicon ships but Huawei's own AI cloud is not compounding. Net margin 7.7 percent.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-huawei-tsmc-die-bank
chunks.text: SemiAnalysis estimated Huawei had received more than 2.9 million Ascend dies from TSMC, a stockpile expected to deplete within about nine months from September 2025. CSIS (2025-04-14) separately reported Huawei obtained approximately 2 million chiplets from TSMC through shell companies for Ascend 910 processors. Huawei's 2025-26 Ascend volume is a stockpile drawdown, not a domestic manufacturing achievement. CORROBORATOR DEMOTED TO A BRACKET 2026-07-25: CSIS says Huawei tricked TSMC into manufacturing '2 million computer CHIPLETS' for the Ascend 910; SemiAnalysis says '>2.9M Ascend DIE'. Chiplets are not dies and the 910 is not the 910B/910C mix — different unit, different generation, so this is a 2M-2.9M bracket (a ~45% spread), not corroboration. Both are hedged. That spread sits on the single most load-bearing number in the 'Huawei is drawing down a stockpile, not manufacturing' argument. The ~9-month depletion timing is SemiAnalysis's alone.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-humain-gpu-commitment-claim
chunks.text: HUMAIN announced plans to deploy up to 600,000 of NVIDIA's latest AI infrastructure technologies across Saudi Arabia and the United States over three years. HUMAIN is a PIF subsidiary launched 2025-05-13. Also announced: a 3 billion USD xAI investment, 211 land plots with access to 14 GW of power, 1.9 GW installed by 2030 and 6 GW by 2034. HUMAIN publishes no audited capacity and PIF does not break out the subsidiary, so none of these figures is verifiable. Log as company claim. The press release says 'up to 600,000 of NVIDIA's latest AI INFRASTRUCTURE TECHNOLOGIES' — a deliberately vaguer unit that may include CPUs, networking and rack-scale systems, not 600,000 accelerators. STRIPPED FROM NOTES 2026-07-25 because none of it is in the cited release: '$23 billion of technology agreements', 'a $3 billion xAI investment', '211 land plots with access to 14 GW of power', '1.9 GW installed by 2030 and 6 GW by 2034'. What the release DOES say: ~18,000 GB300s in the first xAI cluster, and AWS deploying up to 150,000 NVIDIA GPUs in a Riyadh 'AI Zone'. HUMAIN (a PIF subsidiary) publishes no audited capacity and PIF does not break out the subsidiary.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-iea-rare-earth-downstream-risk
chunks.text: The IEA estimates full implementation of China's expanded rare-earth export controls would put about 6.5 trillion USD per year of downstream production outside China at risk. Sectors: automotive, high-tech, defence, energy. Battery-grade graphite disruption would put over 300 billion USD per year at risk. Top-refining-country average share rose to 72 percent in 2025 from 70 percent in 2023 - concentration is still increasing, with rare earths the one exception. Critical-minerals investment fell 9 percent in 2025; battery metals over 20 percent; lithium about 40 percent; copper rose 8 percent. NOTES CORRECTED 2026-07-25: they said 'concentration is still increasing, with rare earths the one exception'. The IEA sentence is 'EXCLUDING rare earths, the average share of the top refining country rose to 72% in 2025, up from 70% in 2023' — rare earths are excluded from the CALCULATION, which is not a finding that rare-earth concentration fell.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-india-ai-mission-budget
chunks.text: India's IndiaAI Mission was sanctioned in March 2024 at Rs 10,371.92 crore, about 1.25 billion USD over five years, of which Rs 4,563.36 crore is for compute. PRIMARY LOCATED 2026-07-25, and it carries only ONE of the three recorded figures. The PIB Cabinet release states the Rs 10,371.92 crore outlay and lists the seven components by name with NO allocation figures, no time horizon and no USD. The five-year horizon is in a companion PIB release the same evening. The Rs 4,563.36 crore compute pillar is in NEITHER — it is in a MeitY Rajya Sabha reply (USQ 1668, answered 2026-02-13), which carries the full pillar table. NO USD FIGURE IS OFFICIAL ANYWHERE: value 1.25 USD_bn is a conversion at roughly INR 83/USD in March 2024, retained only so sovereign programmes can be compared in one unit — it must never be presented as a sourced figure. SANCTIONED, NOT DISBURSED, and now with the number that proves it: per the same Rajya Sabha reply, roughly Rs 401 crore of Rs 10,371.92 crore — about 3.9 percent — had actually reached the mission in its first two years (Rs 21.79 crore in FY2024-25 against RE Rs 173 crore; Rs 379.15 crore in FY2025-26 as at 2026-02-09 against RE Rs 800 crore; nil against the FY2026-27 BE of Rs 1,000 crore). Government figures as of Feb 2026: more than 38,000 GPUs onboarded (higher than the ~34,000 previously noted from Business Standard), 14 empanelled AI service providers, 12 teams shortlisted for indigenous foundation models, 27 India Data and AI labs established. The reply does NOT contain the Rs 65/GPU-hour rate, which still rests on Business Standard alone.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-japan-sovereign-ai-funding
chunks.text: Japan's METI and NEDO awarded the five-year FRONTia multimodal foundation-model project, covering fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2030, to Noetra Corp. and AIST on 30 June 2026, contracting only fiscal 2026 and 2027 with annual stage-gate reviews thereafter. VALUE NULLED 2026-07-25 BECAUSE NO GOVERNMENT SOURCE PUBLISHES ONE. The two yen figures the corpus carried do not come from METI or NEDO: Tom's Hardware attributes both the JPY 1tn five-year total and the JPY 387.3bn first-year tranche explicitly to ASIA TIMES. The only yen figure in any primary is NEDO's public-call document, which sets the FY2026 budget per proposal at 'in principle no more than JPY 383.4 billion' — an AUTHORISED CEILING, not a commitment, and not the 387.3 recorded. NEDO explicitly leaves the five-year total for the proposer to set, so no five-year total is government-published at all. Two further corrections. Contracts cover FY2026 AND FY2027, not one year, with a stage-gate review each year deciding continuation — the contingency is real and funder-documented, but more generous than 'one committed tranche' implied. And AIST is a CO-AWARDEE on the government's own release (Noetra runs the development track, AIST the exploratory track) — the 'working with AIST' clause dropped in an earlier pass was correct and is restored. DROPPED as unsourced: 'funded through GX Economy Transition Bonds' appears in no METI or NEDO document located; GX appears only as a project objective and as a required applicant declaration. Note the corpus was pushed in both directions by two secondary carriers of the same unsourced pair — an earlier pass corrected USD 6.1bn to 6.2bn on one carrier's authority while another carrier says 6.1bn. Both are conversions of a yen figure no primary contains. THIS FACT MUST NOT CARRY A SOVEREIGN-FUNDING LEAGUE-TABLE BAR until the JPY 1tn figure has a primary. Project detail that IS primary: FRONTia is the public name; kickoff 2026-07-16 with METI, ~400 attendees, on-the-record participants including METI Minister Akazawa, PM Takaichi by video, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, Noetra President Tanba, NEC CEO Morita, Sony Group CEO Totoki, SoftBank CEO Miyakawa, Honda President Mibe and AIST President Ishimura. The 27,500 Rubin GPU / 13,750 Vera CPU / 140 MW hardware spec still rests on Tom's Hardware and techtimes (both T2) — the NVIDIA newsroom slug was not located.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-korea-ai-budget-2026
chunks.text: South Korea allocated KRW 10.1 trillion, about 7.25 billion USD, to AI in its 2026 budget, more than tripling the KRW 3.3 trillion allocated for 2025. Strategy shift to selection and concentration: 10,000 GPUs allocated to top foundation-model teams in one tranche. The National Growth Fund, a five-year KRW 150 trillion sovereign vehicle, approved a KRW 560 billion (about 400 million USD) direct equity investment in Upstage. Needs an MSIT primary source before publication. Within a record KRW 728 trillion total 2026 budget; MSIT administers KRW 5.1tn (~51%). Proposed August 2025, cleared by the National Assembly for FY2026 — so 'allocated' is the correct verb, and this is the one genuinely APPROPRIATED sovereign figure in the geopolitics pass, as opposed to announced or sanctioned. The 10,000-GPU tranche, the KRW 150tn National Growth Fund and the KRW 560bn Upstage equity investment still need their own sources or should be cut from the notes.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-nvda-china-hopper-zero-2026q1
chunks.text: NVIDIA shipped no Data Center Hopper products to China in the quarter ended 26 April 2026, compared with 4.6 billion USD in the same quarter a year earlier. Filed confirmation that the China datacentre GPU channel is closed in both directions - US licensing loosened in January 2026 while Beijing barred foreign AI chips from state-funded datacentres in November 2025.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-nvda-china-market-share-huang-claim
chunks.text: Jensen Huang said in April 2026 that NVIDIA's share of the AI accelerator market in China had fallen to zero. Interested party. Log as opinion. Filed corroboration for the direction of travel: China revenue 9,659M USD to 4,550M USD and zero Hopper datacentre shipments. The ~95% prior share is widely repeated but is NOT in this source, whose strongest statement is 'the company owned the lion's share of China's AI accelerator market just two years ago'. Do not restore it without a primary. Huang also said US policy 'has already largely backfired'. The filed language that supports the direction is NVIDIA's own 10-Q: 'we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing market.'

chunks.heading: capita-geo-nvda-china-revenue-2026q1
chunks.text: NVIDIA reported 4,550 million USD of revenue from customers headquartered in China including Hong Kong in the quarter ended 26 April 2026, down from 9,659 million USD a year earlier. Total revenue 81,615 million USD, so China fell from 21.9 percent to 5.6 percent of revenue. Revenue is booked by customer headquarters location, not shipping destination. Add the filing's own caveat: 'Revenue by geographic region is designated based on the location of the headquarters of DIRECT customers. The end customer and shipping location may be different.' Taiwan is $12,006M in the same table — so $4,550M is NOT a China-destination measure, which matters for how this is framed in the surprise list.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-nvda-h20-charge-2025q1
chunks.text: NVIDIA took a 4.5 billion USD charge in the quarter ended April 2025 for excess H20 inventory and purchase obligations after the US required licences for H20-class chips. The cost of a single export-control reclassification to one vendor. Licences were subsequently granted from August 2025.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-nvda-h200-license-zero-revenue-2026-05
chunks.text: NVIDIA had generated zero revenue under the February 2026 H200 China licensing programme as of its May 2026 filing and did not know whether any imports would be allowed into China. Licences require US-based inspection before shipment, so any licensed H200 is subject to a 25 percent tariff on importation into the United States. Supply was legalised; demand remains banned by China.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-qwen-hf-derivatives-2026
chunks.text: Alibaba's Qwen models accounted for the largest model ecosystem on Hugging Face with over 100,000 derivatives as of March 2026. Same USCC paper reports an a16z partner's rough estimate that 80 percent of US startups use Chinese base models to build derivatives, and that Airbnb uses Qwen for customer-service chatbots. China's State Council Information Office claimed 1,509 open model releases in a July 2025 briefing. Carry USCC's own methodology warning: 'some trackers count finetuned variants and derivatives as distinct models, which can dramatically inflate totals.'

chunks.heading: capita-geo-smic-advanced-capacity-2025
chunks.text: SemiAnalysis conservatively estimated SMIC advanced-node capacity at 45,000 wafers per month by end-2025, of which at most 20,000 was needed for Huawei Ascend production. SMIC discloses no 7nm capacity, yield or node mix. Financial Times reported (via TrendForce, 2025-08-29) that SMIC plans to double 7nm capacity in 2026, sourced to unnamed people. SMIC runs 7nm on DUV multi-patterning with no EUV access, so yield rather than capacity is the binding constraint. INVALID CORROBORATOR REMOVED 2026-07-25: the TrendForce/FT item gives no wafers-per-month figure at all — only 'plans to double its 7-nanometer production capacity next year', sourced to unnamed FT sources. A doubling with no baseline cannot corroborate 45,000 wpm. The figure is SemiAnalysis's alone. Adjacent, non-corroborating: FT (unnamed sources, Aug 2025) reported SMIC plans to double 7nm capacity in 2026, no baseline given.
