chunks.heading: capita-geo-smic-capacity-utilisation-2025
chunks.text: SMIC monthly capacity exceeded 1 million standard logic 8-inch-equivalent wafers at end-2025 with utilisation of 93.5 percent, up 8 percentage points year on year. Q1 2026 revenue 2,505.5 million USD (+0.7 percent QoQ), gross margin 20.1 percent; Q2 2026 guidance +14-16 percent QoQ revenue at 20-22 percent gross margin. Selling everything it can make at margins that barely fund the next node. INVALID CORROBORATOR REMOVED 2026-07-25: SMIC's Q1 2026 release contains no capacity or utilisation figure of any kind — only Q1 revenue $2,505.5M (+0.7% QoQ), GM 20.1%, and Q2 guidance +14-16% QoQ at 20-22% GM. It corroborated the notes, not the claim. Also: SMIC does not state whether 93.5% is the full-year average or the Q4 exit rate — the source gives it as a year-over-year comparison.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-smic-revenue-2025
chunks.text: SMIC reported 2025 revenue of 9,327 million USD, up 16.2 percent year on year, at a 21.0 percent gross margin. Net profit attributable to shareholders 685 million USD (+39.0 percent); EBITDA 5,256 million USD; R&D 774 million USD or 8.3 percent of revenue. SMIC's entire annual revenue is under a quarter of TSMC's 2025 capex of 40.9 billion USD, at a gross margin 39 points lower.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-stargate-uae-phase1-mw
chunks.text: G42 and partners announced Stargate UAE as a 1 GW compute cluster inside a 5 GW UAE-US AI Campus, with a first phase of 200 MW targeted for 2026. Company press release - a claim, not verified capacity. Partners G42, OpenAI, Oracle, NVIDIA, SoftBank Group, Cisco; NVIDIA GB300 systems, quantity undisclosed; campus spans 10 square miles; tri-fuel power from Barakah nuclear, utility solar and gas backup. December 2025 reporting put first phase completion in Q3 2026 with long-lead equipment procured and over 5,000 workers on site. Policy counterpart: UAE moved to Country Group A:5 effective 2026-07-10.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-taiwan-blockade-cost-rhodium
chunks.text: Rhodium Group estimated that a Chinese blockade halting all Taiwan trade would put well over 2 trillion USD of global economic activity at risk. Rhodium explicitly calls this 'a conservative and partial estimate', excluding second-order effects, military escalation costs and sanctions. Components: Taiwan annual trade 922 billion USD, value-added trade at high risk 565 billion USD, semiconductor-dependent industries 1.6 trillion USD of potential annual revenue loss. Bloomberg's figures are paywalled at source and are kept as a disputed_by rather than a separate fact. Neither model uses 2025 AI-era trade weights - a genuine gap. The two estimates measure different things: Rhodium's >$2tn is economic ACTIVITY AT RISK; Bloomberg Economics' figure is a FIRST-YEAR GDP LOSS, and its blockade number is 'up to 5%' recorded as 'roughly'. Not averaged, correctly.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-taiwan-energy-import-dependence-2026
chunks.text: Taiwan imports about 97 percent of its energy annually and holds roughly two weeks of emergency supply without new imports. Semiconductors consume roughly 10 percent of Taiwan's energy; industry overall more than half of electricity consumption. Taipower generates almost 80 percent of its electricity from imported fuel. Nuclear was 2.38 percent of the 2024 mix after the last Maanshan unit shut in May 2025; the August 2025 restart referendum failed the turnout threshold; Maanshan safety inspections take 18-24 months with generation possible from about 2028. Taipower accumulated losses 2022-2024 exceeded NT$350 billion (11.08 billion USD). The grid fails before the cleanrooms in any blockade scenario.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-taiwan-sub-10nm-share-rhodium
chunks.text: Rhodium Group put Taiwan's share of the world's most advanced logic chips below 10 nanometres at 92 percent. Same report: TSMC makes 35 percent of the world's automotive microcontrollers and 70 percent of smartphone chipsets. 2022-dated; TSMC's own 2025 filing shows every fab at 5nm and below except Arizona is in Taiwan, so the direction of the estimate is unchanged. Rhodium's $922bn is specifically goods and services traded IN 2021; the notes render it as 'Taiwan annual trade 922 billion USD' with no year.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-tsmc-advanced-node-wafer-rev-share-2025
chunks.text: Advanced technologies of 7 nanometres and below accounted for 74 percent of TSMC total wafer revenue in 2025, up from 69 percent in 2024 and 58 percent in 2023. 2025 split: 3nm 24 percent, 5nm 36 percent, 7nm 14 percent. 2-nanometer entered volume production in 2025; A16 risk production expected in 2026.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-tsmc-annual-capacity-2025
chunks.text: TSMC annual capacity exceeded 17 million 12-inch-equivalent wafers in 2025, and the company shipped 15.0 million 12-inch-equivalent wafers. Shipments 15,022 thousand in 2025 vs 12,910 thousand in 2024 and 12,002 thousand in 2023. Capacity was approximately 17 million in 2024; the 2025 increase came primarily from 3-nanometer expansion.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-tsmc-capex-guidance-2026
chunks.text: TSMC guided 2026 capital expenditure to between 52 and 56 billion USD, after 40.9 billion USD in 2025. Value is the midpoint of the 52-56 billion USD guided range. 2025 capex NT$1,272,411 million = US$40,895 million; 2024 NT$956,007 million; 2023 NT$949,817 million. 2026 spend targets 2nm and 3nm at Fab 20, Fab 21 and Fab 22, plus advanced packaging at Fab 24.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-tsmc-customer-concentration-2025
chunks.text: TSMC's ten largest customers accounted for 78 percent of net revenue in 2025, with the largest at 19 percent and the second largest at 17 percent. Top-ten share was 70 percent in 2023 and 76 percent in 2024. Second-largest customer jumped from 12 percent (2024) to 17 percent (2025) while the largest fell from 22 to 19 percent. TSMC does not name them. TSMC's 20-F says its top-ten customers accounted for 'APPROXIMATELY, 70%, 76% and 78%' — the claim states them as exact.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-tsmc-gross-margin-2025
chunks.text: TSMC gross margin was 59.9 percent in 2025, up from 56.1 percent in 2024 and 54.4 percent in 2023. Q1 2026 gross margin 66.2 percent on net revenue of 35.90 billion USD, per TSMC's quarterly results page. Compare SMIC at 21.0 percent for FY2025. The Q1-2026 66.2% GM on $35.90bn revenue in the notes is not in the cited 20-F and carries no citation — add the TSMC quarterly-results source or split it into its own fact.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-uae-country-group-a5-2026-07
chunks.text: BIS moved the United Arab Emirates from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 to Country Group A:5 effective 10 July 2026, granting the UAE Government and approved entities licence-free access to advanced computing items. Named approved entities in Supplement 8 to Part 740 include G42 (incl. G42 Cloud Technology LLC), Core42 and MGX. No GPU quantity cap appears in the rule text. Rule cites 1 trillion USD of UAE FDI in the US as rationale. Same month China received a 50-percent-of-US-volume cap. TWO CORRECTIONS 2026-07-25. (1) MGX IS NOT AN APPROVED SUPPLEMENT-8 ENTITY — the notes listed it as one. The rule says only that BIS 'intends to favorably review' export licence applications involving MGX; it still requires licences. The UAE-side listings are G42 (incl. G42 Cloud Technology LLC) and Core42 only. (2) OMITTED SUNSET, and it is the strongest qualifier on this fact's 'UAE gets no cap while China gets 50%' contrast: 'Note 2 to paragraph (b): Absent subsequent notice by BIS, the authorization provided for G42 and Core42 in this supplement shall automatically expire on April 6, 2027.' Supplement 8(c) separately lists eight US-headquartered AI companies and their subsidiaries (Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI Group PBC, Oracle, X.AI) — the rule is a US-cloud-in-the-Gulf authorisation as much as a UAE one.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-us-china-ai-capex-gap-2026
chunks.text: Bloomberg Intelligence estimates the four largest US hyperscalers spend more than 400 billion USD on AI capital expenditure in 2026, while spending by five named Chinese cloud providers stays flat from a 2025 base below 40 billion USD. 2025 comparison in the same paper: at least 350 billion USD for Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Google combined versus less than 40 billion USD for Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, SenseTime and Kingsoft Cloud. Keep both China estimates; do not average. The five Chinese cloud providers Bloomberg counts are Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, SenseTime and Kingsoft Cloud. VIZ COLLISION: expert-buildout-us-ai-capex-2025 also carries 400 USD_bn, for all US AI capex in 2025 — same number, adjacent year, different scope. Any chart placing both on one axis will read as flat US capex.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-us-datacenter-projects-blocked-2026q1
chunks.text: Data Center Watch counted 75 US data centre projects worth about 130 billion USD blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026, the largest single-quarter concentration on record. Roughly matching all of 2025 in three months. Active opposition groups rose from 396 at end-2025 to 833 by March 2026, spanning 49 states; over 500,000 Americans in opposition groups across at least 40 states. More than 300 state-level data centre bills filed in the first six weeks of 2026; 14 states introduced statewide moratorium proposals. Stated drivers: electricity prices, water use, noise. Underlying report is by an advocacy-adjacent tracker - treat the count as an estimate. The 'largest single-quarter concentration on record' superlative is Data Center Watch's own, about its own dataset, with no published counting method — attribute it inside the claim ('Data Center Watch describes this as...') rather than asserting it.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-usg-revenue-share-expectation-15pct
chunks.text: US government officials expressed an expectation of receiving 15 percent or more of revenue from licensed NVIDIA sales to China, but no regulation codifying the requirement was published. Verbatim from NVIDIA's 10-Q: 'the USG did not publish a regulation codifying such requirement.' Confirmed absent from the January 2026 rule text, which I read in full. A sovereign revenue share operating on verbal expectation.

chunks.heading: capita-geo-veu-revocations-china-2025-09

chunks.heading: capita-goog-anthropic-200bn-contracts-2026-08
chunks.text: Google has assembled a financing programme tying together contracts worth about $200 billion to supply more than $150 billion of AI chips to Anthropic, with roughly four-fifths of the contract value tied to the chips themselves. Sourced to people involved plus corporate filings reviewed by the FT; the aggregate is the FT's assembly, not a single disclosed figure.

chunks.heading: capita-goog-backed-cost-of-capital-2026
chunks.text: Data centre projects backed by Google borrowed at a median rate of 7.1 per cent, against 9.3 per cent for neocloud operators building around NVIDIA chips — a gap Jefferies analysts called a structural cost-of-capital disadvantage. A 220 bp spread purchased entirely by whose credit stands behind the lease. The clearest evidence on the site that cost of capital, not chip performance, is now a competitive variable.

chunks.heading: capita-goog-backstop-44bn-marked-815mn-2026-08
chunks.text: Google has backstopped 10 data centre developments totalling 2.4 GW of power for TPUs, putting it on the hook for as much as $44 billion if all the leases go bad, while marking the liability at $815 million on its balance sheet. The recognised liability is about 1.9% of the maximum exposure — a 54x gap between contingent obligation and carried value. This is the clearest single illustration on the site of why balance-sheet leverage understates committed obligation in this layer.

chunks.heading: capita-hyperion-bond-2025-10
chunks.text: Meta and Blue Owl issued approximately $27 billion of A+ rated bonds plus about $2.5 billion of equity through a joint-venture SPV arranged by Morgan Stanley in October 2025, anchored by PIMCO. ARRANGER CORRECTED 2026-07-25: previously 'a PIMCO-led private placement' over a bare bloomberg.com domain. PIMCO was the anchor INVESTOR (~$18B), BlackRock ~$3B; Morgan Stanley arranged. JV agreement 2025-10-21; Blue Owl funds 80% / Meta 20%; Blue Owl cash contribution ~$7B; Meta took a one-time distribution of ~$3B. Hyperion campus, 2,250 acres, northeast Louisiana. This also RESOLVES the 80/20 split previously parked in unverified.md for capita-meta-blueowl-jv-2025-10 — it is corroborated and can move onto the site.

chunks.heading: capita-hyperscaler-capex-ms-3500bn-2026-2028

chunks.heading: capita-jpm-stargate-loan-2025-05
chunks.text: A JPMorgan-led lender group provided a $7.1 billion construction loan in May 2025 to the Crusoe-Blue Owl joint venture developing the second phase of the Abilene, Texas Stargate campus, which Oracle leases. TWO LOANS WERE CONFLATED AND THE BORROWER WAS WRONG. The $2.3B JPMorgan construction loan financed Abilene Phase 1 and dates to late 2024 / January 2025; May 2025 was the $7.1B Phase 2 facility, taking JPMorgan's commitment to the site above $7B. The borrower in both cases is the Crusoe / Blue Owl / Primary Digital joint venture — NOT OpenAI, which the previous claim named. This correction is load-bearing: the capital-loop argument is about whose balance sheet carries the leverage, and it is not OpenAI's. Previous source was a Wikipedia URL with an empty quote_ref. If the Phase-1 loan is wanted it becomes a separate fact at as_of 2025-01.

chunks.heading: capita-meta-blueowl-contributions-2025-10
chunks.text: Meta contributed $4.3 billion and Blue Owl $7.0 billion in cash at the formation of their joint venture in October 2025, with Meta taking a one-time distribution of $2.6 billion and holding a 20 percent interest. Split out 2026-07-25. $11.3bn is what was actually capitalised at formation — against a $27bn headline that is total estimated DEVELOPMENT COSTS funded pro rata over time. The gap between the two is the whole point of the structure, and it was uncitable while it lived in notes. Operating leases commence 2029, initial commitment ~$12.3bn over four years, renewals to 20 years, and a residual value guarantee for the first 16 years effectively beginning at $28bn.

chunks.heading: capita-meta-blueowl-jv-2025-10
chunks.text: Meta and Blue Owl Capital formed a joint venture in October 2025 to co-develop the Richland Parish, Louisiana data center campus, committing to fund pro rata shares of approximately $27 billion in total estimated development costs. RE-SCOPED 2026-07-25 against Meta's own filings (the CNBC primary 403s). $27bn is TOTAL ESTIMATED DEVELOPMENT COSTS funded pro rata over time — NOT the JV's size or capitalisation. Capital actually contributed at formation was $11.3bn: Meta $4.3bn, Blue Owl $7.0bn cash, with Meta taking a one-time $2.6bn distribution. TWO ITEMS PREVIOUSLY PARKED IN unverified.md ARE NOW T1-CONFIRMED and can go on the site: the 80/20 split (Meta 20%, Blue Owl 80%), and the leaseback structure — operating leases commence 2029, initial commitment ~$12.3bn over a four-year term, renewals up to 20 years, plus a residual value guarantee for the first 16 years effectively beginning at $28bn and decreasing. The Venture is an unconsolidated VIE under the equity method. Worth its own fact: Meta discloses maximum exposure to loss of $45.95bn against a $1.83bn equity carrying value — a cleaner illustration of off-balance-sheet AI-capex leverage than the $27bn headline. (The FY2025 10-K does not name Blue Owl, saying only 'the Venture'; the 10-Q is the filing that ties the name to the deal.)

chunks.heading: capita-meta-blueowl-max-exposure-2025

The Venture is an unconsolidated VIE under the equity method; no RVG liability had been recorded as of 2025-12-31. This ratio is a cleaner illustration of off-balance-sheet AI-capex leverage than the $27bn headline.

chunks.heading: capita-openai-compute-commit-total
chunks.text: Sam Altman said in November 2025 that OpenAI had about $1.4 trillion of data center commitments, covering roughly 30 gigawatts of capacity over about eight years. AGGREGATION METHOD DELETED 2026-07-25. This was typed as a sum ('Method: sum of Oracle 300 + Microsoft 250 + AWS 38 + AMD/NVIDIA/Broadcom GW deals') sourced to a Wikipedia article, and the method was defective three ways: the cited addends total $588B not $1,400B, so ~$800B was unverifiable under the site's own citation rules; it folded in NVIDIA's up-to-$100B investment INTO OpenAI, counting inbound equity as an outbound purchase; and Oracle's $300B is largely delivered through Stargate sites that carry their own $500B headline, so the sum double-counts. It is not a derived total — it is Altman's own attributed figure. ANY VIZ SHOWING THIS AS A STACKED SUM OF THE CITED DEALS IS MISLEADING and must be rebuilt or relabelled. The site's separately cited contracts account for $588B of it; the balance is not publicly itemised.

chunks.heading: capita-openai-revenue-2025

The old number was ~35% low against the metric it claimed to be. The corpus's headline contrast — $1.4T of commitments against revenue — must name which denominator it uses AND state that the commitments run about eight years, or it silently compares an eight-year total to a single year.

'IN TALKS' HAD BEEN LAUNDERED INTO A COMPLETED BORROWING. The previous claim recorded a $10B facility as done; that was a margin loan collateralised by SoftBank's OpenAI shares, sought in April 2025 at ~7.88%, cut to $6B in May 2025 when lenders balked at valuing private shares, and STILL in renewed talks as of 2026-07-01 with a SoftBank repayment guarantee attached — unclosed fifteen months on. It was also a different facility from the real April 2025 event recorded here. The unclosed margin loan is an excellent fragility datapoint but only as its own, labelled fact. chunks.heading: capita-wulf-2030-secured-notes-3200mn-2025-10

Supersedes an earlier entry that dated this to October 2026 — a future month — by reading the article's 'in October' as its own year. The filing settles it: 22 October 2025. The FT calls the instrument a construction bond and puts the campus at 360 MW; the filing calls it senior secured notes and puts the Fluidstack leases at 378 MW of critical IT load. Prefer the filing on both. The 7.75 per cent coupon sits above the 7.1 per cent median the FT reports for Google-backed projects and below the 9.3 per cent for NVIDIA-orbit neoclouds.

chunks.heading: capita-wulf-abernathy-sale-530mn-2026-07
chunks.text: TeraWulf agreed in July 2026 to sell its entire 50.1 per cent interest in the Abernathy joint venture — a 168 MW campus in Abernathy, Texas — to a purchaser group led by its own tenant Fluidstack for approximately $530.0 million in cash payable in instalments across 2026 and 2027, at a premium to invested capital. TeraWulf had put roughly $450m into the JV. The buyer being the tenant is the structurally interesting part: Fluidstack is simultaneously TeraWulf's largest customer and the acquirer of its assets.

chunks.heading: capita-wulf-backstop-asset-515mn-2025
chunks.text: TeraWulf recorded a $515.5 million asset in deferred charges for the fair value of the warrants issued to Google at issuance, to be amortised straight-line over the life of the Fluidstack leases as the benefit of the backstop is recognised. The clearest number in the corpus for what a credit rating costs when you have to buy one. TeraWulf capitalised its own creditworthiness as an intangible and is depreciating it like a transformer.

chunks.heading: capita-wulf-google-warrant-fv-loss-2026q2
chunks.text: TeraWulf recognised a $755.7 million loss in the quarter to 30 June 2026 and $972.0 million for the half year on the change in fair value of the Google warrants, against nil in the prior-year periods, carrying warrant liabilities of $1,816.7 million at 30 June 2026 versus $844.7 million at 31 December 2025. Non-cash, and it moves the wrong way for the obvious reason: the better the equity story, the larger the loss booked on the warrants sold to buy the guarantee. The liability nearly doubled in six months.

chunks.heading: capita-wulf-google-warrants-73580000-2025
chunks.text: In consideration for Google backstopping Fluidstack's obligations, TeraWulf issued Google warrants over 73,580,000 shares of common stock at an exercise price of $0.01, expiring in August 2030, and Google pledged those warrants to the lenders on the $3,200.0 million notes until the backstop becomes effective. Against 485,734,901 weighted average shares in the quarter. The FT describes these as penny warrants; the filing reserves that term for a 2023 lender issue and calls these the Google Warrants. The pledge is the tell — the guarantee had to be collateralised to the bondholders before it was even live.

chunks.heading: cloud-big4-capex-2025-actual
chunks.text: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spent a combined $376.1 billion of cash capital expenditure in calendar 2025, or $406.4 billion including finance-lease additions. CORRECTED 2026-07-25. The previous $388B came from a Substack whose own per-company figures sum to 378, not 388, and matched no definition. From the filings: MSFT 83.10 / GOOGL 91.45 / AMZN 131.82 / META 69.69 = $376.06B cash capex; +$30.35B of finance-lease ROU assets obtained = $406.41B. The lease-inclusive reading is independently corroborated twice: Bridgewater states $410B, and Tom's Hardware's '$725B in 2026, up 77%' implies a $409.6B base. Any 2025-to-2026 growth rate derived from the old $388B changes.

chunks.heading: cloud-big4-capex-2026-guided
chunks.text: Combined 2026 capital expenditure guidance for Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta reached approximately 700-725 billion USD by mid-2026, versus approximately 630 billion USD as guided in February 2026. Sum-of-guidance estimate; components moved up between Feb and Jun 2026. Both figures kept per disputed-claims rule. RANGE, NOT GUIDANCE: three different estimates exist — Bridgewater $650B, Futurum $690B, Tom's Hardware $725B (an author aggregation of company guidance, not a guided number). Presenting '$700-725B guided' takes the top of a $650-725B spread and calls a forecast guidance. Anchor it instead to the filed datapoint: Q1 2026 actual combined capex was $129.75B, annualizing to ~$519B — every one of those forecasts needs a further 25-40% intra-year ramp. Corroboration named but not linked (moved out of corroborated_by 2026-07-25 so the corroboration count reflects only checkable entries): Silicon Analysts ~$700B guidepoint. Capture the URLs before Gate 3.

chunks.heading: cloud-big4-capex-da-ratio
chunks.text: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta ran combined capital expenditure of $433.9 billion in the trailing four quarters to March 2026, approximately 2.9 times their $149.2 billion of depreciation and finance-lease amortization. REBUILT FROM FILINGS 2026-07-25 (was 'approximately 3x' from a Substack; the digest had hardened that to '3:1'). Trailing 4Q to 2026-03-31, differenced from the 10-Qs: capex $433.90B (MSFT 97.23 / GOOGL 109.92 / AMZN 151.00 / META 75.75). TWO QUALIFIERS MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS NUMBER. (1) The $149.23B denominator is depreciation PLUS finance-lease ROU amortization and EXCLUDES intangible amortization; include intangibles ($155.98B) and the ratio is 2.78x. Add finance-lease ROU assets obtained to the numerator ($465.8B) and it is 3.12x. (2) Amazon is 47% of the denominator on a bundled caption ('depreciation and amortization of property and equipment and capitalized content costs, operating lease assets, and other') carrying ~$16-19B/yr of capitalized video content — stripping non-PP&E items pushes the ratio ABOVE 3x, which is the strongest steelman FOR the depreciation-wall argument and is currently unused. Microsoft's finance leases are ~27% of its capex ($25.99B ROU obtained vs $97.2B cash), so any cash-only series understates the company most exposed to the thesis. Pick one definition, state it once in the methodology note, use it everywhere.

chunks.heading: cloud-fluidstack-tenant-google-recognition-2025-08
chunks.text: Fluidstack USA I Inc. is the named tenant on TeraWulf's 378 MW of Lake Mariner leases, and under recognition agreements Google backstops Fluidstack's payment and performance obligations: on a payment default or insolvency, Google may either pay the lease termination fee or pay all rent due and assume the lease as tenant. The precise legal shape of the arrangement the FT renders as a lockbox diagram. Note the second option: Google can step into the lease itself, which is why the landlord's bondholders treat this as Google credit rather than Fluidstack credit.

chunks.heading: cloud-h100-reserved-rebound
chunks.text: One-year reserved H100 contract pricing bottomed at $1.70 per GPU-hour in October 2025 and rebounded about 38 percent to $2.35 by March 2026. SOURCE UPGRADED 2026-07-25 to SemiAnalysis, the owner of the H100 1-Year Rental Price Index — the Value Add VC post was downstream of it, which removes the T3-needs-corroboration exposure. CAUSATION CORRECTED: the previous notes attributed the rebound to 'inference demand plus HBM cost inflation (~+30% in Q4 2025)'. Both halves were wrong. The memory driver in the index owner's own analysis is LPDDR5 and DDR5 contract prices spiking toward 4-5x YoY in Q1 2026, forcing OEMs to reprice AI servers — system memory, not HBM, and a different magnitude and quarter; the '+30% HBM in Q4 2025' figure exists only in the Value Add VC piece as an unrelated standalone datapoint, and the two memory stories had been fused. And the demand driver is agentic-workload token consumption, not inference — SemiAnalysis explicitly notes H100 TRAINING demand remained strong. The proximate cause both sources agree on is reserved-market supply constraint: providers sold out, little Hopper coming off contract. DO NOT corroborate with Silicon Data's H100 index — that series is on-demand/spot ($2.00 on 2025-12-09 -> $2.20 on 2026-01-06), a different metric; pairing them would be exactly the definition-mismatch failure the brief warns about.

Trane Technologies completed its acquisition of LiquidStack on 2026-03-03 (price undisclosed): https://www.liquidstack.com/news/trane-technologies-completes-acquisition-of-liquidstack — the immersion-cooling pioneer pivoted to direct-to-chip CDUs, then sold to an HVAC major.

chunks.heading: datace-msft-fairwater-size-2025
chunks.text: Microsoft's Fairwater AI datacenter in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin comprises three buildings with 1.2 million square feet under roof on a 315 acre site, built with 46.6 miles of foundation piles and 26.5 million pounds of structural steel. Company claims. Also: 120 miles of MV underground cable, 72.6 miles of mechanical piping, closed-loop liquid cooling with 172 twenty-foot fans; Microsoft claims >90% of capacity uses water only once at construction. Performance claims ('10X fastest supercomputer', 'hundreds of thousands of GPUs') are marketing — not logged as facts.

chunks.heading: datace-nvda-800vdc-2027
chunks.text: NVIDIA announced an 800 volt DC power distribution architecture entering production in 2027 alongside Kyber rack systems, supporting rack densities from 100 kilowatts to more than 1 megawatt. The announcement itself is fact; vendor-claimed benefits (up to 5% end-to-end efficiency gain, 45% less copper, up to 30% TCO reduction) are NVIDIA claims. Ecosystem partners include Vertiv, Schneider Electric, Eaton, Delta, TI, Infineon, ST.

chunks.heading: datace-nvda-copper-busbar-1mw-rack
chunks.text: A 1 megawatt rack using legacy 54 volt DC distribution requires up to 200 kilograms of copper busbar per NVIDIA's engineering analysis. Vendor engineering estimate used to justify the 800 VDC transition; 'up to' framing. At 54V, power shelves would also consume up to 64 rack units at megawatt scale.

chunks.heading: datace-rack-power-baseline-2024
chunks.text: Typical air-cooled AI racks in 2022 to 2024 were rated at about 41 kW. Split out 2026-07-25 as the correct before/after anchor for rack-density charts. The corpus had been using 16 kW as the 2022-24 baseline, but Bizo's 16 kW is the magnitude of the power FLUCTUATION (about 4 kW per 8-GPU node), not the rack's power level. The error ran against the corpus's own interest: it manufactured a 9x escalation to 150 kW where the true one, 41 kW to 150 kW, is real and sufficient. Source URL is the Uptime journal root; the exact article slug was not captured and should be recovered before publication.

chunks.heading: datace-tt-ai-liquid-premium-2025
chunks.text: US liquid-cooled AI data centers cost 7 to 10 percent more to construct than air-cooled facilities of equivalent IT capacity in 2025. Value is the midpoint of the 7-10% range given by the source; consultancy benchmark, method not fully published.

chunks.heading: datace-tt-cost-escalation-2025
chunks.text: The cost per watt of building a traditional air-cooled data center rose 5.5 percent in 2025, versus 9.0 percent reported the prior year. For 2026, 60% of surveyed respondents expect cost increases of 5-15% and 21% expect more than 15% (same source).

chunks.heading: datace-tt-cost-per-watt-tokyo-2025
chunks.text: Tokyo was the most expensive data center construction market in 2025 at 15.2 USD per watt, followed by Singapore at 14.5 and Zurich at 14.2. Benchmarks for traditional cloud, air-cooled builds. US markets: Silicon Valley $13.3/W (4th), New Jersey $12.9/W (5th), Portland $10.9/W. Survey of over 280 industry experts across 52 markets.

chunks.heading: datace-tt-power-obstacle-2025
chunks.text: 48 percent of the more than 280 data center industry experts surveyed cited power availability as the most prominent obstacle to delivering projects on schedule in 2025. Long grid-connection lead times named as main constraint. Power strategy split: 44% grid + diesel backup, 28% redesigning power architecture for density, 14% exploring alternative/on-site power. Also: 73% of leaders view the sector as recession-proof (same survey, landing page). Survey base: over 280 experts across 52 markets and more than 300 live or recent projects. Two loose ends: the note's '60% expect 5-15% cost increases and 21% expect more than 15%' for 2026 is on none of the four report pages fetched — locate or trim; and the methodology page carries a July 2026 copyright with an FX window of 2024-10-01 to 2025-10-01, so the 2025-11-05 source date on all four datace-tt-* facts deserves a re-check.

chunks.heading: datace-uptime-ai-power-swings-2025
chunks.text: Rack power draw during AI training can swing by more than 100 percent within milliseconds, with GB200 NVL72 racks observed climbing from roughly 60-70 kilowatts to more than 150 kilowatts against a 132 kilowatt specification. Spikes occur every second or two; worst-case instantaneous overshoot up to 20% above spec. Context: Context: typical 2022-24 air-cooled AI racks were RATED ~41 kW, with power FLUCTUATIONS of ~4 kW per 8-GPU node (~16 kW per rack). Correction 2026-07-25: the note previously read Bizo's 16 kW as a rack power LEVEL; it is the magnitude of the fluctuation. The error ran against the corpus's own interest — it manufactured a 9x escalation (16 kW -> 150 kW) where the true one (41 kW -> 150 kW) is real and sufficient. Any before/after viz must use 41 kW as the 2022-24 anchor.

chunks.heading: datace-uptime-dlc-niche-2026
chunks.text: Uptime Institute analyst Jacqueline Davis argued in April 2026 that direct liquid cooling will remain confined to high-density AI and HPC applications and not reach mainstream mission-critical adoption within 3 years. Steelman against cooling-transition hype. Barriers cited: redundant CDU/manifold engineering, reduced ride-through time for generator start, unresolved facilities-vs-IT ownership of DLC components.

chunks.heading: datace-uptime-rack-power-200kw-2026
chunks.text: AI hardware roadmaps point to rack power soon surpassing 200 kilowatts, with GPUs above 2 kilowatts per module and CPUs approaching 1 kilowatt per socket, as of July 2026. RETYPED fact -> forecast 2026-07-25 (so it takes the --forecast/dashed treatment everywhere per CLAUDE.md). The claim asserted a present-tense observation — rack power 'is approaching and in some cases exceeding 200 kW as of mid-2026' — but the source is in the opposite tense: manufacturers are 'planning ever-higher computing density, with a corresponding sharp increase in rack power — soon to surpass 200 kW'. 'In some cases exceeding' has no basis in the article at all. The recorded quote_ref was also a paraphrase formatted as a quotation and has been replaced with the verbatim line. Flow-rate note verified ('keep flows under 1.5 liters per kilowatt per minute at 10C rise'). UNVERIFIED: the note's 'Jensen Huang has proposed 45C supply water; two-phase targets ~50C' did not surface in the article — locate its real source or trim.

chunks.heading: datace-vrt-backlog-2025
chunks.text: Vertiv's estimated combined order backlog was 15.0 billion USD as of December 31, 2025, up from 7.2 billion USD as of December 31, 2024. Backlog more than doubled in one year, now ~1.5x annual revenue. 10-K: majority firm and expected to ship within 12-18 months; orders being placed in advance of ability to fulfill; customers can reduce/defer usually with penalties.

chunks.heading: datace-vrt-guidance-2026
chunks.text: Vertiv guided full-year 2026 net sales to 13,500-14,000 million USD with organic sales growth of 29 to 31 percent. Value is the guidance midpoint. Company's own forecast, raised at Q1. Adjusted operating margin guided 22.8-23.8%; adjusted FCF $2.1-2.3bn.

chunks.heading: datace-vrt-net-sales-2025
chunks.text: Vertiv reported net sales of 10.2 billion USD for fiscal year 2025, with 58 percent transacted in the Americas, versus 8.01 billion USD in 2024. FY2025 regional split per 10-K: 58% Americas, ~24% APAC, 18% EMEA.

chunks.heading: datace-vrt-q1-sales-2026
chunks.text: Vertiv reported Q1 2026 net sales of 2,650 million USD, up 30 percent year over year, with 44 percent organic growth in the Americas and a 20.8 percent adjusted operating margin. 23% organic + 4% acquisitions + 3% FX. Adjusted operating margin +430bps YoY 'inclusive of tariff impacts' — pricing power evidence. Net leverage ~0.2x; investment-grade ratings Feb 2026.

chunks.heading: datacen-goog-crypto-miner-conversion-2026
chunks.text: The Financial Times identified five crypto-miner data centre projects totalling 1.4 GW of power that raised $15 billion of debt with the support of a Google backstop, converting miners with secured power into AI infrastructure developers. Confirms this layer's verdict that the scarce input is a megawatt with a date on it: what made these miners valuable was secured power, not compute.

chunks.heading: datacen-wulf-anthropic-19bn-contracted-2026-07
chunks.text: TeraWulf's 20-year Anthropic lease at the Justified Data Campus is reported to carry approximately $19 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term. Typed as an estimate deliberately: the 10-Q discloses the megawatts, the term and the extension options but not the contract value, so the $19bn traces to the company's own announcement and the press carrying it rather than to a filing. Treat the MW and the term as facts and this as a company figure until a filing repeats it.

chunks.heading: datacen-wulf-anthropic-401mw-20yr-2026-07
chunks.text: TeraWulf signed a lease with Anthropic PBC in July 2026 to provide approximately 401 MW of critical IT load at the Justified Data Campus in Hawesville, Kentucky, on an initial 20-year term with two five-year extension options at Anthropic's election, with initial capacity expected in the second half of 2027 and full delivery in early 2028; the lease had not commenced as of the filing date. Unlike the Lake Mariner leases, no Google backstop is disclosed for this one. That is the single most consequential open item on the company.

chunks.heading: datacen-wulf-energized-102mw-2026-07
chunks.text: TeraWulf had energized 102 MW of critical IT high-performance computing capacity at the Lake Mariner campus as of July 2026. The gap between this and the contracted 378 MW plus 401 MW is the whole execution question. Energized megawatts are the only number on this page that cannot be signed into existence.

chunks.heading: datacen-wulf-fluidstack-378mw-lake-mariner-2025-08
chunks.text: TeraWulf's subsidiary Akela signed three data centre leases with Fluidstack USA I Inc. in August 2025 covering 378 MW of critical IT load at the Lake Mariner campus, the majority of the campus's remaining contracted capacity; one had partially commenced by 30 June 2026 and the rest are expected to commence in the second half of 2026 and early 2027. The FT reports 360 MW, which matches the earlier announced capacity before Fluidstack exercised an option for additional load. The filing figure is the current one.

chunks.heading: datacen-wulf-revenue-netloss-2026q2
chunks.text: TeraWulf reported total revenue of $44.8 million for the quarter to 30 June 2026, of which $31.9 million or 71 per cent was HPC lease revenue and $12.8 million was digital asset revenue, against a net loss of $940.8 million. The crossover quarter: lease revenue passed mining revenue for the first time, while total revenue fell year on year because bitcoin revenue fell faster than leases ramped. The net loss is roughly 21 times revenue and is mostly the warrant mark, not operations.

chunks.heading: datasu-cloudflare-default-block
chunks.text: Cloudflare, serving about 20 percent of the web, made AI-crawler blocking the default for new domains on July 1, 2025 Company's own press release — 20%-of-web is a company claim. >1M customers had opted to block AI crawlers since Sept 2024; 50+ publishers backing; pay-per-crawl in private beta at launch.

chunks.heading: datasu-consent-crisis
chunks.text: Between April 2023 and April 2024, 5 percent or more of all C4 tokens and 28 percent or more of tokens from its most actively maintained critical sources became robots.txt-restricted, with 45 percent of C4 restricted when Terms of Service are included 14,000-domain audit across C4, RefinedWeb, Dolma. The measured web-crawl enclosure baseline; predates Cloudflare's 2025 default-block.

chunks.heading: datasu-mercor-expert-economics
chunks.text: Mercor pays expert contractors 60-70 percent of top-line revenue at average rates above $85 per hour with over $2 million of daily payouts as of mid-2026 30,000+ weekly active contractors. Marks the shift from cents-per-annotation commodity labeling (Scale) to expert-hour economics for RL-era data. The 60-70% contractor revenue share and the $85+/hour average are Sacra-only, and the corpus uses that ratio to net Mercor's $2B gross down to ~$600-800M annualized — that arithmetic rests entirely on an uncorroborated ratio. TechCrunch independently corroborates only the payout scale ($1.5M/day to 30,000+ experts, Oct 2025).

chunks.heading: datasu-mercor-runrate-2026
chunks.text: Mercor reached $2 billion of annualized gross revenue in June 2026, up from a $760 million run-rate at end-2025 GROSS revenue — contractors keep 60-70% of top line, so net take is ~$600-800M annualized. Customers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta. Independently corroborated by Forbes (2026-07-09): 'crossed $2 billion in annualized revenue in June, doubling its sales four months after hitting $1 billion in February' — so it stays type:fact despite Sacra's hedge, and the $1B/Feb-2026 waypoint fills the $760M-end-2025 -> $2B-Jun-2026 gap. Not a fact, worth a note: Mercor was in talks to raise $500M at $20B, expected to close late July 2026. (Forbes misdates the Series C to September 2025; Oct 27-28 2025 is correct.)

chunks.heading: datasu-mercor-series-c
chunks.text: Mercor raised a $350 million Series C at a $10 billion valuation on October 28, 2025 Series B $100M at $2B (Feb 2025); $486M total raised through 2025; FCF-profitable early 2026.

chunks.heading: datasu-r1-synthetic-tokens
chunks.text: DeepSeek-R1's reinforcement-learning phase generated approximately 2 trillion synthetic tokens Scale reference: one RL run self-generated ~13% as many tokens as V3's entire 14.8T-token pretraining corpus — synthetic data substituting for scraped data at the margin.

chunks.heading: datasu-scale-customer-exodus
chunks.text: Google, which spent about $150 million with Scale AI in 2024 and had planned $200 million for 2025, moved to split from Scale after the June 2025 Meta investment. July 2025: Scale laid off 200 FTE (~14%) and ended ~500 contractor relationships. Neutrality = the moat in labeling; Meta stake broke it. DEPARTURE LANGUAGE SOFTENED 2026-07-25: the originating CNBC report says Google 'plans' a split (intent, not completion) and states that OpenAI's CFO said the company WILL CONTINUE working with Scale as one of several data vendors — so 'OpenAI: Departed' was contradicted by its own source. Microsoft was reported to be pulling back; xAI looking to exit. The dollar figures are corroborated; the completeness of the departures is not. The 'neutrality was the moat' verdict still stands on the July 2025 layoffs (200 FTE, ~500 contractors).

chunks.heading: datasu-scale-layoffs-2025-07
chunks.text: Scale AI laid off 200 full-time employees, about 14 percent of staff, and ended roughly 500 contractor relationships in July 2025. Split out 2026-07-25 from the notes of datasu-scale-customer-exodus. This is what actually carries the layer's 'neutrality was the moat' verdict — the customer-departure framing turned out to be overstated (OpenAI's CFO said publicly it would keep working with Scale), so the layoffs one month after the Meta stake are the surviving evidence. It was in a note while the overstated version was in the claim.

chunks.heading: datasu-scale-meta-deal
chunks.text: Meta invested $14.3 billion for a 49 percent non-voting stake in Scale AI at a $29 billion valuation in June 2025 Widely reported (Reuters/CNBC June 2025); Sacra was the fetchable source this session. Announced 2025-06-12, closed 2025-06-13; valuation reported as ~$29B-$29.2B.

chunks.heading: datasu-scale-revenue
chunks.text: Scale AI reported $870 million of 2024 revenue with a $1.5 billion annualized run-rate at end-2024 and an estimated $2 billion in 2025 Labeling economics per same source: per-task markup to 50%+ gross margin; 2 cents/image, 6 cents/annotation.

chunks.heading: datasu-surge-raise-2025
chunks.text: Surge AI was reported in July 2025 to be in talks for its first outside capital, up to $1 billion, at valuations reported between $15 billion and $25 billion. NO CLOSE REPORTED as of July 2026, twelve months on — do not state 'Surge is a $25B company'. Sacra's page carries two valuations from two outlets: 'exceeding $15 billion' (Reuters) and 'at least $25 billion' (Bloomberg); the corpus previously recorded only the top of that spread and typed an unclosed round as fact. Large secondary component reported, with J.P. Morgan facilitating founder/employee sales. Secondary sources now float $20B and $24B marks.

chunks.heading: datasu-surge-revenue-2024
chunks.text: Surge AI reached $1.2 billion of annualized revenue in 2024 while bootstrapped and profitable since its 2021 launch 130 FTEs, ~50,000 expert contractors; 12 frontier-lab customers (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Microsoft, Meta) = >$1B of it. Extreme customer concentration. No independent source exists — Surge is private and bootstrapped, and every hit restates Sacra. Also Sacra-only: 130 FTE, ~50,000 contractors, 12-customer concentration.

chunks.heading: distrib-acn-bookings-q3fy26
chunks.text: Accenture reported new bookings of 19.32 billion USD in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, a decrease of 2 percent in US dollars and 3 percent in local currency, on revenue of 18.7 billion USD, with approximately 799,000 employees. Consulting bookings $10.26bn, Managed Services $9.06bn. Prior quarters: Q1 FY26 bookings $20.94bn (+12% USD), Q2 FY26 $22.11bn (+6% USD). Full-year FY26 revenue growth guidance cut to 3%-4% in local currency; FY26 GAAP diluted EPS guided $13.38-$13.50. Bookings declined year-over-year in the quarter AI consulting was supposedly compounding — the core tension in the SI half of this layer.

chunks.heading: distrib-acn-genai-bookings-discontinued
chunks.text: Accenture disclosed no generative-AI bookings or revenue figure in any of its three fiscal-2026 quarterly earnings releases, the terms generative AI and GenAI appearing zero times in each. value null / unit not_disclosed because the finding IS the absence. Verified by extracting text from all three T1 PDFs with pdftotext and grepping case-insensitively for 'generative' and 'genai': zero hits in each. Consequence for the corpus: end-acn-genai-bookings-fy2025 ($5.9bn) and end-acn-genai-share-bookings-fy2025 (7.3%) are TERMINAL FY2025 values, not a live series, and should be labelled as such on the layer page.

chunks.heading: distrib-acp-launch-no-gmv
chunks.text: Stripe and OpenAI launched the Agentic Commerce Protocol on 29 September 2025 with Etsy as the first integrated merchant, disclosing no transaction volume, no fee schedule and no governance body. value null / unit not_disclosed deliberately: the announcement is a capability claim with no volume attached. Initially US-only, US merchants only, Etsy live and Shopify 'coming soon'. The core primitive is a Shared Payment Token scoped to one merchant and one amount. Stripe calls ACP 'an open standard' but names no standards body, no committee and no spec-management process — a contrast worth drawing against MCP, which moved to the Linux Foundation in December 2025. Reporting that OpenAI retired Instant Checkout in March 2026 in favour of dedicated retailer apps came only from inadmissible aggregator pages; see research/unverified.md, because if true it is the most important datapoint in this sub-section.

chunks.heading: distrib-adobe-ai-first-arr-q2fy26
chunks.text: Adobe reported that AI-first annual recurring revenue tripled year over year and exceeded 500 million USD in its second fiscal quarter of 2026, against quarterly revenue of 6.62 billion USD. $500m of ARR against roughly $26.5bn of annualised revenue is about 1.9% — the smallest AI share among the incumbents that disclose one (Salesforce Agentforce ~2.7% of annualised revenue; Microsoft's $37bn AI run rate against ~$300bn+). It is also the fastest-growing of the three. 'AI-first ARR' is an Adobe-defined metric with no published composition; the release states the figure without a breakdown by Firefly, Acrobat AI Assistant or enterprise. No SAP AI-specific ARR or seat disclosure was located this session.

chunks.heading: distrib-adobe-ai-referral-conversion
chunks.text: Adobe Analytics reported that AI-referred traffic to US retail sites grew 138 percent year over year in May 2026 and converted at a rate 54 percent better than non-AI traffic, reversing a position a year earlier when AI conversion was roughly half that of non-AI sources. Adobe's proprietary panel (more than 1 trillion visits to US retail sites); Adobe's own blog posts on this data timed out repeatedly this session, so the citation is the secondary report and confidence is medium. Adobe sells AI marketing tooling, so the incentive to emphasise AI channel performance is real — flag it. Also reported: +1,324% since October 2024; 53% more time on site; 23% more pages per visit. An earlier snapshot put the conversion advantage at 42% in March 2026, consistent with the trajectory rather than in conflict. Significance: agents already route consumer demand at measurable scale while the protocols built to monetise that routing report no volume at all.

chunks.heading: distrib-ap2-partner-count
chunks.text: Google announced the Agent Payments Protocol on 16 September 2025 with more than 60 partner organizations and disclosed no transaction volume. Stated as a floor ('more than 60'), so value 60 is a lower bound. Extends A2A and MCP; payment-agnostic across cards, stablecoins, real-time bank transfers and crypto; addresses authorization, authenticity and accountability for agent-initiated purchases. Named partners include Mastercard, American Express, PayPal, Adyen, Coinbase, Worldpay, Ant International, Intuit, JCB, UnionPay International, Revolut, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Etsy, Forter and Mysten Labs. Two competing agent-payment standards launched within 13 days of each other in September 2025, neither with any disclosed volume ten months later.

chunks.heading: distrib-aws-marketplace-private-offer-tiers
chunks.text: AWS Marketplace private-offer listing fees fall from 3 percent below 1 million USD total contract value to 2 percent between 1 and 10 million USD and 1.5 percent at or above 10 million USD, with all renewals at 1.5 percent. The rake regresses toward zero exactly where the money is. A large enterprise AI contract renewed through AWS Marketplace pays 1.5%; professional services private offers pay 0.5%. Conclusion for the layer: hyperscaler marketplaces do not exert App-Store-style pricing power. Their distribution power comes from committed-spend drawdown, not from the take rate.

chunks.heading: distrib-aws-marketplace-saas-vs-server-fee
chunks.text: AWS Marketplace charges a 3 percent listing fee on public software-as-a-service offers and a 20 percent listing fee on public server offers including machine images and containers, effective 5 January 2024. Fees computed on pre-tax Total Contract Value. The near-7x spread between deployment models means an AI vendor's packaging choice — hosted service versus customer-run container — changes its platform tax more than any negotiation would. Also on the same page: +0.5% uplift for channel partner private offers; +1% regional uplift for South Korea buyers effective 2025-04-01.

chunks.heading: distrib-aws-profserv-fee-cut
chunks.text: AWS reduced the AWS Marketplace listing fee on professional services private offers from 2.5 percent to 0.5 percent, effective 16 June 2026. An 80% fee cut, applying to new private offers only. Read as a bid to pull system-integrator implementation work — the AI-services spend documented elsewhere in this layer — onto the AWS transaction rail. Note that Microsoft moves the opposite way on services: professional services are explicitly NOT eligible for Azure consumption commitment drawdown.

chunks.heading: distrib-capgemini-genai-bookings-share-2025
chunks.text: Capgemini reported that generative AI contributed more than 8 percent of group bookings in 2025 and more than 10 percent in the fourth quarter, on total bookings of 24,356 million euros. Company-defined metric in an earnings release — a company claim, and stated as a floor ("more than") rather than a point value, so value 8 is a lower bound. Revenue EUR 22,465m (+1.7% reported, +3.4% constant FX); book-to-bill 1.08. Capgemini is now the only major SI still publishing an AI share of bookings: it exceeds Accenture's terminal FY2025 7.3% and, unlike Accenture's, is still being reported. FY2026 guidance +6.5% to +8.5% constant FX.

chunks.heading: distrib-capgemini-headcount-2025
chunks.text: Capgemini employed 423,400 people at 31 December 2025, an increase of 82,300 or 24 percent year over year, with 279,200 or 66 percent of headcount offshore. Direct evidence against the 'AI collapses SI headcount' story in the same year GenAI passed 8% of bookings. The 24% jump reflects the WNS acquisition alongside organic hiring, so it is not a pure organic-hiring signal — but the direction is unambiguous and it matches Cognizant (+21,300 YoY). Pair with distrib-hcl-ai-deflation-guidance: the named executives are guiding to price compression, not headcount collapse.

chunks.heading: distrib-cognizant-headcount-bookings-q1-2026
chunks.text: Cognizant reported trailing-twelve-month bookings of 29.6 billion USD, up 11 percent, and headcount of 357,600 at 31 March 2026, up 21,300 year over year, with no AI-specific revenue or bookings figure disclosed. Q1 2026 revenue $5.413bn (+5.8% USD, +3.9% cc); FY26 guidance $22.11-22.64bn; 7 large deals signed at or above $100m TCV including one at or above $500m; 'over 70% large deal total contract value growth'. Cognizant markets itself as an 'AI builder' and isolates no AI revenue. The headcount direction is the load-bearing datapoint: the second-largest US-listed SI added 21,300 people in the year AI was supposed to be deflating its labour model.

chunks.heading: distrib-hcl-ai-deflation-guidance
chunks.text: HCLTech chief executive C. Vijayakumar said AI deflation would reduce revenue by three to five percent in the coming year, in the same reporting round in which Tata Consultancy Services reported a 0.5 percent annual revenue decline. Typed opinion because it is forward-looking executive commentary, attributed by name, with value null plus value_range per the schema rule for ranges. This is the steelmanned fragility case for the services channel and it is a claim about PRICE, not volume: TCS CEO K. Krithivasan called the same effect 'degrowth' against a 0.5% annual revenue decline described as TCS's first contraction since its 2006 listing; Wipro CFO Aparna Iyer flagged 'lower margins in some deals' on +4% FY26 revenue. Not primary-verified against the companies' own releases — TCS investor PDFs return 403 to automated fetches.

chunks.heading: distrib-infosys-fy26-no-ai-revenue
chunks.text: Infosys reported fiscal 2026 revenue of 20,158 million USD, up 3.1 percent in constant currency, with large-deal total contract value of 14.9 billion USD, and disclosed no AI-specific revenue, bookings or contract-value figure anywhere in the results release. Infosys describes itself in the same release as "a global leader in AI-first business consulting and technology services" and CEO Salil Parekh's quotes rest entirely on AI positioning ("enterprise AI value proposition", "AI First value framework", "differentiated Topaz Fabric") — while every AI mention in the document is positioning or a named-client anecdote, never a number. FY27 guidance 1.5%-3.5% constant currency, operating margin 20%-22%. Q4 revenue $5,040m (+4.1% cc YoY, -1.3% QoQ). Free cash flow $3,733m. TCS's widely-cited $2.3-2.6bn annualised AI run rate could not be primary-verified (tcs.com PDFs return 403); see research/unverified.md.

chunks.heading: distrib-m365-copilot-list-value-estimate
chunks.text: At the 30 USD per user per month list price, Microsoft's 20 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats imply approximately 7.2 billion USD of annualised list value, roughly 19 percent of Microsoft's disclosed 37 billion USD AI run rate. MY DERIVATION, not a Microsoft disclosure: 20,000,000 x $30 x 12 = $7.2bn. It is a CEILING and almost certainly above realised ACV: enterprise agreements at that volume are discounted, E5 and Business Premium bundling shifts revenue attribution between SKUs, and Microsoft has never confirmed that Copilot revenue sits inside the $37bn AI run rate as defined. Confidence low. Presented only to bound the gap between the seat headline and the revenue headline — the point being that seats are the loudest Copilot number and dollars are the quietest.

chunks.heading: distrib-m365-copilot-paid-seats
chunks.text: Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella said Microsoft 365 Copilot had more than 20 million paid enterprise seats as of the quarter ended 31 March 2026, up from 15 million one quarter earlier. SEATS SOLD, NOT SEATS USED — and disclosed verbally on the earnings call only. The FY26 Q3 press release contains no Copilot seat count at all, which is why confidence is medium rather than high despite the CEO attribution. Supporting colour from the same call, all unaudited: Copilot queries per user up ~20% quarter-over-quarter; weekly engagement 'at the same level as Outlook'; the count of companies buying more than 50,000 seats has quadrupled; Bayer, Johnson & Johnson, Mercedes and Roche each above 90,000 seats; Accenture bought over 740,000 seats, Microsoft's largest Copilot win to date.

chunks.heading: distrib-macc-100pct-drawdown
chunks.text: One hundred percent of the pretax purchase amount of an Azure-benefit-eligible partner offer bought through Microsoft Marketplace decrements the customer's Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment. The most under-covered real mechanism in layer 14: it turns a third-party AI purchase into a zero-marginal-cash decision for any enterprise already carrying an Azure commitment, while a direct purchase requires new budget. The conditions are the moat: the purchase must be made through Marketplace inside the Azure portal on a subscription tied to the agreement (credit-card purchases on marketplace.microsoft.com do NOT count); Azure prepayment is ineligible; the licence must be used exclusively in Azure, so hybrid or on-prem deployment breaks eligibility; professional services are ineligible; CSP-routed deals do not decrement MACC; and MACC eligibility itself requires the vendor to attain Azure IP co-sell eligible status. Distribution power built out of accounting, not product.

Same release: Microsoft Cloud revenue $54.5bn (+29%); Azure and other cloud services +40%; Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud +19%; commercial remaining performance obligation $627bn (+99%), superseding the corpus's $625bn figure at 2025-12-31. Note the RPO growth rate decelerated from +110% to +99% across one quarter while the absolute number barely moved ($625bn to $627bn).

chunks.heading: distrib-msft-csp-no-reseller-margin

The workarounds it does document are Multiparty Private Offers and Resale Enabled Offers, where Microsoft pays the selling partner and the ISV separately. Critical interaction with MACC: CSP-routed deals close outside Marketplace and therefore do NOT decrement a customer's Azure commitment, so the reseller channel and the committed-spend channel are mutually exclusive for the same deal. A claimed 10 percent global-distribution-channel incentive for IP co-sell SaaS partners could not be located in a primary page; see research/unverified.md.

chunks.heading: distrib-msft-marketplace-service-fee

Agency model: the customer contracts with Microsoft under their Microsoft Customer Agreement or Enterprise Agreement; Microsoft owns billing, collections, tax and payout while the publisher sets price and terms. Private-offer renewals get a 50% fee discount. Google Cloud Marketplace's equivalent rate could NOT be verified this session — its fee documentation page 404'd; see research/unverified.md. Do not assume parity.

chunks.heading: end-mit-pilot-stall-2025
chunks.text: About 5 percent of custom enterprise generative AI tool efforts were judged successfully implemented in MIT NANDA's July 2025 preliminary report. THREE CORRECTIONS 2026-07-25, all against the MIT PDF itself. (1) METHODOLOGY WAS WRONG: notes said '150 interviews, 350 employee survey, 300 public deployments'. The report says a review of over 300 publicly disclosed AI initiatives, structured interviews with representatives from 52 ORGANIZATIONS, and survey responses from 153 SENIOR LEADERS collected at four industry conferences — two of three figures off by ~3x and ~2x, and the survey population is senior leaders at conferences, not employees. (2) 'RAPID REVENUE ACCELERATION' IS FORTUNE'S PHRASE, absent from the report; MIT defines success as tools causing 'a marked and sustained productivity and/or P&L impact'. (3) FRAMING: the report is dated July 2025, self-labelled 'Preliminary Findings', carries a disclaimer that the views 'do not reflect the positions of any affiliated employers', and self-limits ('directionally accurate based on individual interviews rather than official company reporting... success definitions may differ'). The site was presenting it as an MIT study of comparable rigour to Menlo's survey.
