The nearest sourced version of a duplication story is Latitude Media's 'phantom load' framing, but that is Nov-2025/226 GW vintage and rests on unnamed 'industry experts suspect', which the constitution forbids. What the ERCOT decks actually describe is a different mechanism: pre-batch study invalidation and restudy loops from the absence of capacity reservation. (2) ARITHMETIC: the notes said 'roughly 7x ERCOT's ~86 GW peak load'. It is ~5.1x — 438,000 MW / 85,508 MW (the all-time peak of 2023-08-10, stated in the same document). The digest and surprise #2 must use 5.1x. ercot.com is Incapsula-blocked to automated fetch; re-check via web.archive.org.

chunks.heading: grid-ercot-peak-load-record
chunks.text: ERCOT's all-time peak demand record was 85,508 MW, set on 10 August 2023. Split out 2026-07-25 so the queue-to-peak ratio can be cited arithmetic rather than an assertion. 438,000 MW of large-load queue divided by this figure is ~5.1x — the corpus previously said ~7x, and the corrected number was sitting in another fact's notes where no page could cite it. Same ERCOT document as grid-ercot-large-load-queue-gw.

chunks.heading: grid-ercot-queue-growth-gw
chunks.text: ERCOT's large-load interconnection queue grew from 63 GW at end of 2024 to 226 GW in November 2025. From ERCOT filing ahead of its December 2025 board meeting; ~77% of the 226 GW was data centers targeting connection by 2030. Notes corrected 2026-07-25: the data-center share was recorded as ~77%; ERCOT's own Board deck says ~73% of the 226 GW. The 226 and 63 GW values are exact. Data date is 2025-11-18. Unused ERCOT framing: 'Large Load MW demand seeking interconnection by 2030 has grown by 142 GW (270%) since the beginning of 2025.'

chunks.heading: grid-ferc-pjm-colo-order
chunks.text: FERC ordered PJM on December 18 2025 to create four transmission service options for co-located large loads, finding the existing tariff unjust and unreasonable. Options: NITS, interim non-firm, firm contract-demand, non-firm contract-demand. Generators delisting capacity for co-located load must fund all reliability upgrades before reducing capacity; BTM netting restricted via materiality threshold. Rates filing due 2026-02-16. FERC.gov page 403'd this session; law-firm summary used.

chunks.heading: grid-ferc-showcause-rtos
chunks.text: FERC issued show-cause orders on June 18 2026 to all six FERC-jurisdictional RTOs and ISOs requiring them to justify or revise large-load interconnection rules within 60 days. Proposed elements: >=50 MW large-load threshold, hourly forecast and telemetry requirements, pro forma cost-recovery agreements so large-load customers bear network-upgrade costs. 30 days: generation adequacy report.

chunks.heading: grid-ferc-talen-isa-rejection
chunks.text: FERC rejected the amended Talen-Amazon interconnection service agreement for expanded behind-the-meter supply from the Susquehanna nuclear plant on November 4 2024. Value = the 480 MW expansion sought (from 300 MW); 2-1 vote and commissioner reasoning behind paywall — see unverified.md. The ruling that pushed co-location deals front-of-meter.

chunks.heading: grid-gas-equipment-easing
chunks.text: Wood Mackenzie vice chair Ed Crooks said in February 2026 that GE Vernova, Siemens and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries have all announced significant gas-equipment capacity expansions since the start of 2025. Named expert (Ed Crooks, Wood Mackenzie). Steelman against the permanent-equipment-scarcity narrative: supply is responding, first in gas turbines. Attribute fully: Ed Crooks, Wood Mackenzie Vice Chair of AMERICAS. The unused half of this source is a steelman against the L1 digest's 'the turbines are the constraint' framing — Crooks says gas turbine manufacturers are 'increasingly not the primary bottleneck' for large loads seeking power.

chunks.heading: grid-gs-5yr-peak-gw
chunks.text: Aggregate US utility 5-year summer peak load growth forecasts filed with FERC reached 166 GW by 2030 in 2025 filings, up six-fold from 24 GW in 2022 filings. Progression of FERC Form 714-based forecasts: 2022: 24 GW, 2023: 38 GW, 2024: 64 GW, 2025: 166 GW. Peak +3.7%/yr, energy +5.7%/yr, total use +32% by 2030. PDF read directly.

chunks.heading: grid-gs-dc-overstatement-gw
chunks.text: Grid Strategies estimates the data center portion of utility load forecasts is overstated by roughly 25 GW, as market analysts indicate data center growth is unlikely to require much more than 65 GW through 2030. This is the key steelman against the demand-tsunami narrative, made by the same analysts who document the tsunami. Drivers of overstatement: duplicate requests, unrealistic load factors (some near 100%), timing optimism. MISSING COUNTER-STEELMAN 2026-07-25: the corpus uses Grid Strategies' 40%-overstatement finding as the bull-case steelman but omits the counter-steelman published in the same report — 'Utility forecasts of 2022-2025 growth were revised UP, not down... load growth increased from a forecast 18 GW to an actual 25 GW (~35%)', plus 'PJM is evaluating forecast adjustments which could add as much as 27 GW to its 2030 load forecast'. Presenting only the overstatement half gives the fragility claim a one-sided steelman.

chunks.heading: grid-gs-dc-share-gw
chunks.text: Roughly 90 GW of the 166 GW of forecast US peak load growth through 2030 is linked to data centers, about 55 percent. Industrial/manufacturing ~30 GW, oil & gas/mining ~10 GW, other drivers ~30 GW. Method: Grid Strategies interpretation of utility forecast subsector detail covering ~90% of national load.

chunks.heading: grid-gs-region-growth-gw
chunks.text: Six regions account for over 80 percent of forecast US five-year load growth: ERCOT 53 GW, PJM 30 GW, SPP 24 GW, MISO 16 GW, Georgia Power 8 GW, CAISO 7 GW. Value field = ERCOT (largest). PJM growth driven by Northern Virginia data centers; ERCOT by data centers, industry and oil & gas.

chunks.heading: grid-imm-dc-auction-cost-bn
chunks.text: PJM's independent market monitor attributes 29.4 billion dollars of the 63.6 billion dollars in total capacity charges across the last four auctions to data centers, including 6.3 billion of 16.4 billion in the July 2026 auction. 46% of four-auction total; 38% of latest auction. IMM proposes separate capacity auctions for data centers. Method: IMM counterfactual attribution — inherently model-based. CORROBORATED EXACT at T1 against the IMM's own slides: '$29.4B, or 46.2 percent of total capacity market charges over those four auctions' and '$6.3B... 38.2 percent' of $16.4B. The four auctions are the BRAs for delivery years 2025/26 through 2028/29 — name them wherever the figure is used. Unused and stronger: the IMM puts the data-center capacity impact at raising H1-2026 wholesale power cost from $103.40 to $114.50/MWh.

chunks.heading: grid-lbnl-dc-2023-twh
chunks.text: US data centers consumed approximately 176 TWh in 2023, about 4.4 percent of national electricity, up from 58 TWh in 2014. Baseline anchor for all demand-growth claims in this layer. Merged duplicate primar-lbnl-dc-load-2023 (independently logged by primary-energy agent) on 2026-07-25.

chunks.heading: grid-lpt-leadtime-months
chunks.text: Large power transformer lead times often exceed 24 months and prices have risen approximately 77 percent since 2019. Weakest-sourced fact in layer: vendor blog relaying Wood Mackenzie (paywalled). Higher circulating figures (128 weeks US average; 44-58 months for 100+ MVA by maker) are SEO-tier only — logged in research/unverified.md. Next step: GE Vernova / Siemens Energy / Hitachi earnings materials (T1).

chunks.heading: grid-miso-dpp-timeline-years
chunks.text: MISO's Definitive Planning Phase interconnection process averaged 3 to 4 years as of February 2025, with a stated goal of a 1-year process by the 2028 cycle. MISO using Pearl Street Technologies automation plus an annual queue cap; launched Consolidated Planning Process March 2026.

chunks.heading: grid-miso-queue-gw
chunks.text: MISO's interconnection queue contained 1,705 projects representing 312 GW of generating capacity as of early 2025. Direct fetch blocked (403); figures taken from accessible search summary of the S&P article — confidence capped at medium.

chunks.heading: grid-msft-pecos-gw
chunks.text: Microsoft announced a 2 GW data center in Pecos, Texas on June 22 2026, with the company funding the energy infrastructure. Company announcement relayed in Utility Dive coverage; exemplar of hyperscalers self-funding grid infrastructure to bypass queues.

chunks.heading: grid-nerc-level3-alert-mw
chunks.text: NERC issued a Level 3 Essential Actions alert on May 4 2026 on computational load, after observing customer-initiated large load reductions and oscillations that occur within seconds; two data center load-reduction events exceeded 1,000 MW during 2025, the largest 1,800 MW. THREE CORRECTIONS 2026-07-25. (1) 'Level 3 alert' is CORRECT — NERC's own wording, its highest tier, Essential Action to Industry, initial distribution 2026-05-04. (2) 'SUB-SECOND' IS WRONG and must be replaced with 'within seconds' everywhere, including digest surprise #4 — NERC says the reductions 'occur in seconds'. (3) The 1,000+ MW figure is NOT IN THE ALERT at all; it comes from the 2026 State of Reliability, and it is TWO instances in 2025 (largest 1,800 MW, Feb 2025 Eastern Interconnection, caused by a transmission fault; then 1,300 MW in June), with many more above 100 MW — 'repeated events' overstated a count of two. TWO CAVEATS THE CORPUS OMITTED: the alert is explicitly NON-BINDING ('does not create a mandatory obligation... will not be subject to penalties'), and NERC's 'computational load' category includes CRYPTOCURRENCY MINING as well as AI data centers — the ERCOT half of the event record is crypto, not AI.

chunks.heading: grid-nerc-risk-areas
chunks.text: NERC found that 13 of 23 assessment areas face resource adequacy challenges over the next ten years in its 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment. WORDING CORRECTED 2026-07-25: 'potential capacity shortfalls' overstates the majority of the 13. NERC explicitly states Elevated-Risk areas MEET resource adequacy criteria and face shortfall only under extreme conditions; only High-Risk areas exceed shortfall criteria. Based on planned resources as of July 2025. Also DELETED: a note claiming 'over half of US electricity customers exposed to elevated reliability risk' — that sentence does not appear in the LTRA. Was sourced to a PureSky Energy blog recap (T3) of a document that fetches fine. NAMING: this is the 2025 LTRA published January 2026 — grid-nerc-transmission-miles calls it 'the 2025 NERC LTRA' and this fact called it 'the January 2026 LTRA'; they are the same document.

chunks.heading: grid-nerc-summer-peak-gw
chunks.text: NERC's Long-Term Reliability Assessment published January 2026 projects US summer peak demand growth of approximately 224 GW over ten years, nearly 70 percent above the prior year's forecast. Winter peak projected +245-246 GW; a 20-25% nationwide peak increase over the decade. NERC PDF itself returned 403 this session; recap plus Utility Dive corroboration used.

chunks.heading: grid-nerc-transmission-miles
chunks.text: The 2025 NERC LTRA reports 41,000 miles of transmission above 100 kV under construction or in development over the next 10 years, up from 28,275 miles in the 2024 LTRA. Increase is concentrated in planning phases; miles actually under construction have not risen substantially over past-year levels.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-2020cohort-completion-pct
chunks.text: 24 percent of PJM's 2020 interconnection entry cohort reached an interconnection agreement or became operational. ERCOT 2020 cohort: 40%. PJM 2018-2020 cohort: 65-80% of capacity withdrew entirely before executing an agreement. TWO ANNOTATIONS 2026-07-25. (a) These are GENERATION interconnection waits, printed in the L2 digest immediately after 'the bottleneck inverted from generation queues to LOAD queues' — the word 'generation' must appear or a reader takes 40 months as a load-queue wait. (b) The cited page is a press release summarising the white paper 'AI Meets the Grid: Interconnection Queue Analysis in PJM and ERCOT' (2026-05-14), whose underlying data is LBNL 'Queued Up 2025 Edition' — cite the white paper or LBNL.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-auction-2028-price
chunks.text: PJM's capacity auction for the 2028-2029 delivery year cleared at the 325 dollar per MW-day price cap on July 15 2026, totaling 16.4 billion dollars. Uncapped clearing estimated at $555/MW-day RTO-wide ($777 ComEd), ~$29.7B. Prior auction (Dec 2025): ~$329.17/MW-day. NOTES CORRECTED 2026-07-25. The prior-auction price was wrong: notes said 'Prior auction (Dec 2025): ~$329.17/MW-day', but PJM's 2028/2029 BRA report says the 2027/2028 BRA cleared at its cap of $333.44; $329.17 was the 2026/2027 BRA (July 2025). TWO OMISSIONS THAT CHANGE THE DIGEST: PJM states the $16.4B total was 'UNCHANGED from the $16.4 billion value in the 2027/2028 BRA' — the digest implies escalation, and the auction total was flat year over year — and that it 'does NOT equate to a total cost to load because load that is hedged through self-supply or bilateral contracts is not exposed to the clearing prices'. Uncapped simulation: $554.72 RTO, $776.69 ComEd, $29.7B.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-auction-2028-shortfall-gw
chunks.text: PJM's 2028-2029 capacity auction cleared 6.8 GW below its 20 percent installed reserve margin target and attracted 525 MW of new supply. Prior auction shortfall 6.5 GW; new supply fell from 774 MW to 525 MW (208 MW of which were uprates). Forecast demand rose ~2 GW, primarily data centers.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-avg-wait-months
chunks.text: Average interconnection wait time in PJM was 40 months as of May 2026, versus a federal target of 8 to 11 months. National average 25 months; ERCOT average 20 months (gas 17, storage 23, renewables 27). Derived from Carbon Direct analysis of ISO queue data. TWO ANNOTATIONS 2026-07-25. (a) These are GENERATION interconnection waits, printed in the L2 digest immediately after 'the bottleneck inverted from generation queues to LOAD queues' — the word 'generation' must appear or a reader takes 40 months as a load-queue wait. (b) The cited page is a press release summarising the white paper 'AI Meets the Grid: Interconnection Queue Analysis in PJM and ERCOT' (2026-05-14), whose underlying data is LBNL 'Queued Up 2025 Edition' — cite the white paper or LBNL.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-backstop-gw
chunks.text: PJM proposed adding 14.9 GW of capacity through bilateral contracts and central backstop procurement matching large loads with generation sellers in April 2026. Headline-level capture; proposal status at FERC not verified this session.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-cycle1-2026-gas-gw
chunks.text: Gas-fired generation led PJM's reopened interconnection queue with 106 GW as of April 2026. Reversal from renewables-dominated queues of 2020-2024; PJM using Google Tapestry AI tool to process applications. PJM's release: natural gas 105.8 GW across 157 projects. Same nameplate/realisation caveat as grid-pjm-cycle1-2026-queue-gw applies.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-cycle1-2026-queue-gw
chunks.text: PJM's reopened interconnection Cycle 1 drew 811 projects totaling 220 GW of nameplate capacity as of April 2026. 'NAMEPLATE' ADDED and PJM's own realisation caveat recorded 2026-07-25, both previously omitted: 'The gigawatt and megawatt figures represent the MAXIMUM POTENTIAL OUTPUT of a resource into the system. Based on historical performance, ONLY A PERCENTAGE of projects that apply for interconnection will sign interconnection agreements.' The digest's 'PJM reopened after 4 years and drew 220 GW led by gas' reads as pipeline that will be built — it must be presented alongside grid-pjm-2020cohort-completion-pct (only 24% of the 2020 cohort reached an IA). Also: 'reopened after 4 years' is not in PJM's release, which says only 'no remaining backlog from prior queues'. Window closed 2026-04-27.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-queue-closed-years
chunks.text: PJM's interconnection queue was effectively closed to new entrants from 2022 until April 2026. Pre-reform backlog exceeded 2,700 projects with roughly 4-year average waits.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-reform-studied-gw
chunks.text: PJM studied approximately 160 GW of interconnection requests between the July 2023 reform launch and September 2025, with approximately 46 GW remaining for completion by end of 2026. PJM says future generation interconnection agreements will take 1-2 years to issue. Only 2.1 GW of new generation connected in PJM during 2025.

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-shortfall-2030-gw
chunks.text: Ascend Analytics projects a potential PJM capacity shortage reaching 15 GW by 2030 as load additions outpace new generation. Named forecaster: Ascend Analytics. Consistent with growing auction reserve shortfalls (6.5 -> 6.8 GW).

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-transition-cycle1-gw
chunks.text: PJM completed Transition Cycle 1 of its reformed interconnection process in September 2025 with 130 new service requests totaling 17.4 GW of generation output. 56% solar, 25% wind, 10% storage, 5% hybrid, 3% gas; plus 2 merchant transmission projects (~2 GW transfer capability).

chunks.heading: grid-pjm-wholesale-cost-jump-pct
chunks.text: PJM wholesale power costs rose 54 percent in one year per Monitoring Analytics reporting in March 2026. Headline-level capture; article body not fetched this session. Superseded by the same body: the IMM's July 2026 deck states total wholesale power cost increased 50.3% (YTD 2025/2026) against the recorded 54% (March 2026, a different window). Re-anchor and state the window.

chunks.heading: grid-puct-batch-zero-mw
chunks.text: The Public Utility Commission of Texas approved ERCOT's initial large-load interconnection batch-study process on June 18 2026, covering projects of 75 MW or larger. Batch Zero applicants notified Aug 2026; final transmission plan fall 2027; Batch 1 opens summer 2027; most Batch Zero projects expected operational by 2030. ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas: 'fundamental shift'.

chunks.heading: grid-tmi-doe-loan-bn
chunks.text: Constellation secured a 1 billion dollar Department of Energy loan in late 2025 to accelerate the Crane Clean Energy Center restart, with commercial operation targeted around 2027. Restart pulled forward from 2028 to ~2027.

chunks.heading: grid-us-345kv-miles-2024
chunks.text: The US built 888 miles of new 345 kV and above transmission in 2024, versus 322 miles in 2023 and roughly 5,000 miles per year indicated as necessary by the DOE 2024 National Transmission Planning Study. The DOE study benchmark did not incorporate the new load growth, so the ~5,000 mi/yr need is understated relative to 2025 forecasts.

chunks.heading: grid-us-load-factor-pct
chunks.text: The US power system operates at about a 60 percent load factor as of 2025, up from 58 percent three years earlier, and is forecast to reach 66 percent in 2030. Dominion Virginia reported an 82% load factor for large data centers in 2024; Duke Energy plans for 80% on new large loads. Data centers add energy faster than peak.

chunks.heading: infere-anthropic-opus5-output-price
chunks.text: Claude Opus 5 API pricing is $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens as of July 2026. Value is output price. Flagship output price fell $75 (Opus 4.1) to $25/MTok (Opus 4.5 onward) = 3x cut; a new higher tier (Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5) sits at $10/$50. Cache read 0.1x input; batch 50% off; fast mode Opus 5 at $10/$50.

chunks.heading: infere-anthropic-sonnet5-price-increase
chunks.text: Claude Sonnet 5 output price rises from $10 to $15 per million tokens on September 1, 2026, ending introductory pricing of $2/$10 in effect through August 31, 2026. Counterexample to monotonic token-price deflation: a scheduled 50% list increase. Docs also note Claude 4.7+ tokenizer produces ~30% more tokens for the same text, an effective per-request price increase invisible in $/MTok tables.

chunks.heading: infere-baseten-arr-2026-03
chunks.text: Baseten reached $600 million in annualized revenue in March 2026, up from $200 million in December 2025. Series F Jun 2026: $1.5B at $13B (Altimeter, Conviction, Spark). Claims 100x inference volume growth in 2025. Single source (Sacra). A disputed_by entry claiming the ~1,900% growth figure was arithmetically inconsistent has been DELETED as wrong: 1,900% is year-over-year (Mar 2025 ~$30M -> Mar 2026 $600M), while $200M -> $600M is a separate three-month step. Baseten's own Series F post says revenue grew 20x — exactly 1,900%. From the same T1 post: inference volume grew 40x; >1B inference calls/day across 87 clusters and 18 clouds.

chunks.heading: infere-braintrust-pro-price
chunks.text: Braintrust Pro plan pricing is $249 per month including 50,000 scores and 5 GB processed data as of July 2026. Starter $0 (10k scores, 1 GB, 14-day retention). Overages: scores $1.50/1k (Pro) $2.50/1k (Starter); data $3-4/GB; retention $0.50/GB/mo. Evals/observability priced on volume units — revenue scales with layer-11 token throughput.

chunks.heading: infere-daytona-vcpu-price
chunks.text: Daytona Windows sandbox compute is priced at $0.0858 per vCPU-hour as of July 2026. Usage-based; $200 free compute; up to $50k startup credits; sub-90ms sandbox creation is a company claim (not independently benchmarked). Linux per-vCPU rate not explicitly listed on fetched page.

chunks.heading: infere-e2b-pro-price
chunks.text: E2B Pro plan pricing is $150 per month plus usage, with up to 100 concurrent sandboxes and 24-hour session length, as of July 2026. Compute: 1 vCPU $0.000014/s (~$0.05/vCPU-h), RAM $0.0000045/GiB/s; concurrency purchasable to 1,100. Compare Anthropic first-party: 1,550 free container-hours/org/month then $0.05/container-hour — frontier-lab bundling pressure on standalone sandbox vendors. Modal sandbox CPU $0.00003942/core/s = ~3x its standard compute rate.

chunks.heading: infere-fireworks-arr-2026-05
chunks.text: Fireworks AI reached $800 million in annualized revenue in May 2026. ~$305M at end-2025. Series D Jul 2026: $1.505B at $17.5B post (~17.5x revenue). >10,000 customers Oct 2025; ~$28K blended ARR/customer. Single source (Sacra). SUPERSEDED ten weeks later by the company itself: >$1B annualized run rate (fireworks.ai, 2026-07-15) — see infere-fireworks-arr-2026-07. Retain only as a Sacra-estimated waypoint.

chunks.heading: infere-fireworks-arr-2026-07
chunks.text: Fireworks AI surpassed $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate in July 2026. Company-stated (T1), ~5x YoY from ~$305M at end-2025. Supersedes the Sacra-estimated $800M/May-2026 waypoint (infere-fireworks-arr-2026-05). Makes the Series D multiple ~17.5x revenue, not the ~22x the $800M figure implies — check any revenue-multiple line in the inference layer. Also company-stated: >40 trillion tokens/day (from 15T a year earlier), >95% from customer-specialized models.

chunks.heading: infere-fireworks-gross-margin
chunks.text: Fireworks AI gross margin was approximately 50 percent as of mid-2026, with a stated target of 60 percent. Key datapoint against the serving-is-a-commodity thesis: 45-50% gross margins at the managed-platform tier (Together est. ~45%) despite open-weight price parity at the API layer. LOAD-BEARING AND UNCORROBORATED: '~50%, targeting 60%' appears nowhere but Sacra — not in the Series D announcement, the BusinessWire release, or any independent coverage. The corpus's anti-commoditization verdict rests on this plus Together's ~45%, which is also a Sacra-only estimate. Label that verdict 'on Sacra estimates' or soften it.

chunks.heading: infere-gptoss120b-cross-provider-price
chunks.text: Groq serves gpt-oss-120B at $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens at approximately 500 tokens per second as of July 2026. Value is output price. Near-parity pricing on identical open weights across independent providers = commoditization evidence at the open-model API layer. Corroboration named but not linked (moved out of corroborated_by 2026-07-25 so the corroboration count reflects only checkable entries): Baseten serves GPT OSS 120B at $0.10/$0.50 per MTok (baseten.co/pricing, fetched 2026-07-24). Capture the URLs before Gate 3.

chunks.heading: infere-groq-nvidia-headline-total
chunks.text: Press reporting put the total value of NVIDIA's December 2025 Groq licensing deal at about $20 billion, of which $17 billion was cash. Split out 2026-07-25 from the notes of infere-groq-nvidia-license-2025-12 so a page can state the headline and the cash component without conflating them. CNBC and Bloomberg carry ~$20-20.6bn; Axios independently confirms the $17bn cash across three installments (85% up-front, 10% mid-2026, remainder end-2026) with ~$10.3bn to shareholders.

chunks.heading: infere-groq-nvidia-license-2025-12
chunks.text: Groq signed a non-exclusive licensing agreement with Nvidia on December 24, 2025 worth $17 billion in cash across three installments by end of 2026. $7.6B distributed to shareholders Feb 2026 (~$64/share); further $2.7B pending share redemption. Reads as soft exit of the independent-LPU challenger thesis. Groq revenue: $90M (2024), $500M 2025 projection. md). CORROBORATED independently (Axios, 2025-12-28): $17B in cash across three installments (85% up-front, 10% mid-2026, remainder end-2026), ~$10.3B to shareholders — which reconciles Sacra's $7.6B + $2.7B. The press headline total is ~$20-20.6B, of which $17B is the cash. The soft-exit reading strengthens: CEO Jonathan Ross and president Sunny Madra moved to Nvidia; the CFO became CEO.

chunks.heading: infere-h100-cross-provider-spread-2026-07
chunks.text: Published H100 on-demand pricing across four inference providers spanned $3.95 to $7.00 per GPU-hour in July 2026, a spread of about 1.8 times. Split out 2026-07-25 from the corroborated_by of infere-together-h100-hourly, where it was stranded. This is the inference layer's best commoditization evidence and it is unusually clean: four first-party published price lists, same hardware, fetched the same day. A 1.8x spread on identical silicon is the argument that serving is NOT yet a pure commodity, and unlike the layer's gross-margin evidence it does not depend on a single analyst's estimate.

chunks.heading: infere-langchain-arr-2025-06
chunks.text: Fortune reported LangChain's annual recurring revenue at $12 million to $16 million as of June 2025, against the $1.25 billion valuation of its October 2025 Series B. Split out 2026-07-25 from the notes of infere-langchain-valuation-2025-10. This is the sharpest fragility datapoint in the agent-infra layer and it was uncitable, so the page could only say 'no disclosed revenue'. At $12-16M the Series B was struck at roughly 80-100x ARR — in the layer the corpus separately shows being absorbed by the model providers. A spokesperson said ARR had grown since; no updated figure has been published. Layer set to agent-infra rather than inference: LangChain is orchestration, and the original id's infere- prefix reflects which research agent found it, not where it belongs.

chunks.heading: infere-langchain-valuation-2025-10
chunks.text: LangChain was valued at $1.25 billion in its October 2025 Series B of $125 million led by IVP. Total raised $260M; prior round $100M at $1.1B only three months earlier (Jul 2025). Fortune reported LangChain ARR at $12-16M as of June 2025 (spokesperson said it had grown since) — i.e. the $1.25B Series B was struck at roughly 80-100x ARR, a far stronger agent-infra fragility datapoint than the valuation alone. — monetization via LangSmith usage+seat pricing. Single source (Sacra).

chunks.heading: infere-langsmith-plus-seat-price
chunks.text: LangSmith Plus plan pricing is $39 per seat per month as of July 2026. Developer tier $0/seat + usage; Plus includes up to 10k base traces/mo (14-day retention; 180-day extended tier available); consumption billed as LCU $1.50 / LSU $1.00. No flat per-1k-trace list price published.

chunks.heading: infere-mcp-code-exec-token-cut
chunks.text: Anthropic's code-execution-with-MCP worked example reduced agent token consumption from 150,000 to 2,000 tokens, a 98.7 percent reduction, in November 2025. Published Nov 4, 2025. Google Drive-to-Salesforce workflow example; company-published demonstration, not independent benchmark. Same post: "thousands" of community MCP servers since Nov 2024 launch; thousand-tool setups consume "hundreds of thousands of tokens" before work begins. chunks.text: Celestica's operating margin rose from 4.0 percent in 2022 to 8.4 percent in 2025, with gross margin up from 9.0 to 12.1 percent. The one contract manufacturer whose margins expanded rather than compressed through the AI cycle - and it did so by selling its own networking hardware alongside assembly, not by assembling more. Doubling operating margin off a 9% gross margin base is the counter-example to 'assembly cannot improve'. Derived from filed line items.

chunks.heading: system-dell-ai-optimized-server-rev-q1fy2027
chunks.text: Dell Technologies recognised 16,132 million dollars of AI-optimized server revenue in the quarter ended May 1 2026, up 757 percent year over year. In one quarter Dell recognised 65% of its entire prior fiscal year's AI-server revenue.

chunks.heading: system-dell-ai-orders-vs-revenue-q1fy2027
chunks.text: Dell Technologies booked 24.4 billion dollars of AI orders and recognised 16.1 billion dollars of AI server revenue in the quarter ended May 1 2026. The booked/recognised distinction in a single company sentence: $8.3bn of the quarter's orders were not revenue. Dell's 10-K and 10-Q both describe backlog growth qualitatively and disclose no backlog figure.

chunks.heading: system-dell-ai-server-guidance-fy2027
chunks.text: Dell Technologies raised its fiscal 2027 AI server revenue expectation to 60 billion dollars in May 2026. Company guidance by Jeff Clarke (vice chairman and COO), not a filed result. Implies roughly 2.4x the FY2026 figure of $24,683M. Must render with forecast treatment.

chunks.heading: system-dell-ai-server-rev-fy2026
chunks.text: Dell Technologies recognised 24,683 million dollars of AI-optimized server revenue in fiscal 2026, up from 1,873 million dollars in fiscal 2024. 13x in two years. This is recognised revenue, not orders or backlog: Dell reports the two separately (see system-dell-ai-orders-vs-revenue-q1fy2027).

chunks.heading: system-dell-consol-gross-margin-q1fy2027
chunks.text: Dell Technologies' consolidated gross margin was 17.8 percent in the quarter ended May 1 2026, down from 24.3 percent in the quarter ended May 5 2023. 6.5 points of company-wide gross margin given up as AI servers went from a rounding error to 37% of revenue. Derived from filed gross margin over net revenue (SEC XBRL, CIK 0001571996). Dell's consolidated OPERATING margin rose 330bp to 8.3% in the same quarter - the strongest available steelman that scale beats ratio in this layer.

chunks.heading: system-dell-isg-operating-margin-fy2026
chunks.text: Dell Technologies' Infrastructure Solutions Group operating margin fell to 11.7 percent in fiscal 2026 from 12.8 percent in fiscal 2025 and 12.6 percent in fiscal 2024. Segment operating margin declined while segment revenue grew 40% and AI-server revenue grew 166%. Dell's stated cause: 'a decline in gross margin rate as a result of a shift in mix towards our AI-optimized servers offerings.'

chunks.heading: system-dell-isg-operating-margin-q1fy2027
chunks.text: Dell Technologies' Infrastructure Solutions Group operating margin was 10.5 percent in the quarter ended May 1 2026, on 29,009 million dollars of segment revenue. Up 80bp year over year but down from 11.7% for FY2026. Dell's explanation is precise and worth quoting in full on the page: the rise came 'due to a decline in operating expense rate that outpaced the decline in gross margin rate'.

chunks.heading: system-dell-operating-margin-expansion-q1fy2027
chunks.text: Dell expanded consolidated operating margin by 330 basis points to 8.3 percent in Q1 fiscal 2027, while giving up 6.5 percentage points of gross margin. Split out 2026-07-25. THE SYSTEMS LAYER'S HEADLINE STEELMAN, and it was stranded in another fact's notes so the page could only state it qualitatively. It is the strongest argument against 'integration is a pass-through business': Dell surrendered 6.5pp of gross margin on AI-server mix and still expanded the consolidated operating line 330bp, because opex did not scale with revenue. Scale can beat ratio. Note what it is NOT: a pricing-power argument. It is a volume argument, and it requires the volume to continue.

chunks.heading: system-delta-margin-expansion-power
chunks.text: Delta Electronics' operating margin rose from 7.66 percent in 2018 to 15.13 percent in 2025, on gross margin of 34.27 percent. Delta supplies power shelves, busbars and PSUs into rack-scale systems. Doubled operating margin at 4.7x Quanta's level on the same demand. Q1 2026: 37.00% gross, 17.83% operating on NT$159.4bn. CAVEAT: Delta is diversified beyond datacenter power (industrial automation, EV, infrastructure) and does not break out an AI-rack segment, so attribution of the expansion to rack-scale is inferential.

chunks.heading: system-flex-margin-expansion
chunks.text: Flex's gross margin rose from 5.8 percent in fiscal 2019 to 9.2 percent in fiscal 2026, with operating margin from 1.7 to 4.9 percent. Flex is the western contract manufacturer taking challenger rack-scale work (see existing fact sys-cerebras-flex-7x). Its FY2026 4.9% operating margin sits between Quanta's 4.12% and Wiwynn's 6.72%, confirming a narrow global band for merchant assembly regardless of geography or customer. Derived from filed line items.

chunks.heading: system-foxconn-us-footprint-2025
chunks.text: Foxconn said it operates more than 40 facilities across 12 US states and is expanding AI server production in Texas, Wisconsin and California. Company claim in a press release - value 40 is a stated floor, no square footage or investment disclosed, hence medium confidence. Houston is the named site for GB300 tray modules. Chairman Young Liu quoted. Relevant to the Taiwan-concentration question: the US footprint is real but Foxconn discloses no split of AI-rack output by geography.

chunks.heading: system-gb300-nvl72-configuration
chunks.text: The NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 integrates 72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs in one fully liquid-cooled rack with 37 terabytes of fast memory and 130 terabytes per second of NVLink bandwidth. The unit of sale is now a rack, not a server. Vendor specification page (T1 for configuration, not for performance claims). NVIDIA publishes no power, weight or cost figure for GB300 NVL72 - see the GB200 facts for those.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-ai-market-share-claim
chunks.text: Hon Hai's spokesperson said the company has reached around 40 percent market share in the AI market. Company claim with no stated definition of the market, no methodology and no third-party corroboration found. Recorded as opinion, not fact, and must be attributed to James Wu wherever used. Widely repeated second-hand as a 'roughly 40% of AI server rack assembly' share - that specific framing is not what was said.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-ai-rack-shipment-guidance-2026
chunks.text: Hon Hai guided 2026 AI rack shipments to more than double, conditional on supply chain material availability. Company forecast; value 100 encodes '>1x growth' i.e. more than doubling, as a floor. The condition is explicit and load-bearing: Michael Chiang said growth of 'at least more than double' applies 'if supply chain material availability can meet demand'. Same slide: 800G+ switches 2x growth in 2026, CPO switches to mass production in 3Q26.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-ai-server-share-of-server-revenue
chunks.text: Hon Hai stated that AI server revenue exceeded 50 percent of its server revenue in the first quarter of 2026. Company statement, floor not a point - value 50 is the stated lower bound. Chiang gave 'close to 50%' for full-year 2025. No supporting table was published, hence medium confidence.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-buy-and-sell-passthrough
chunks.text: Hon Hai's rotating CEO said many of its businesses use a buy-and-sell model in which product prices are adjusted according to costs. The pass-through model stated by the operator, in answer to a question about whether raw-material cost inflation threatens the 3% operating-margin floor. Chiang's point is that cost shocks have 'relatively limited impact on our absolute profitability' - the layer transmits input shocks straight to the buyer's capex rather than absorbing them. Nothing quantitative is claimed, hence value null / unit not_disclosed.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-capex-2025
chunks.text: Hon Hai's capital expenditure was around 174 billion New Taiwan dollars in 2025, up approximately 27 percent year over year, and it guided to more than 30 percent growth in 2026. Roughly US$5.5bn - the capital cost of the world's largest AI-rack integration network, against NVIDIA's fiscal Q1 2027 supply commitments of $145bn. Q1 2026 capex was NT$35.8bn, down 18% YoY. The >30% 2026 figure is company guidance, not a result.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-cloud-networking-share-q1-2026
chunks.text: Cloud and Networking Products were 48 percent of Hon Hai's revenue in the first quarter of 2026. Against total quarterly revenue of NT$2,119,533M this is roughly NT$1.02tn (~US$32bn) of server and networking revenue in a single quarter. Corroborated verbally on the same call ('Cloud and Networking Products has now approached 50%').

chunks.heading: system-honhai-consignment-model-asic
chunks.text: Hon Hai's CFO said consignment is the main transaction model in its ASIC server projects, reducing working capital, inventory, receivables and payables. CRITICAL METHODOLOGICAL CAVEAT for every margin in this layer. Under consignment the customer owns the silicon, so it never enters the integrator's revenue or cost of sales - the identical physical work reports a HIGHER gross margin on a MUCH SMALLER revenue base. No integrator discloses its buy-and-sell versus consignment mix, so cross-company and cross-year margin comparisons are contaminated by an undisclosed variable. Huang also said the model 'has the opportunity to expand' to GB-series GPU servers as GB200/GB300 mature.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-gross-margin-flat-2018-2025
chunks.text: Hon Hai's consolidated gross margin was 6.15 percent in 2025 versus 6.27 percent in 2018, while revenue rose from 5.29 to 8.10 trillion New Taiwan dollars. Eight years, revenue up 53%, gross margin down 12 basis points. The clearest evidence that scale confers no pricing power in rack and box assembly. Operating margin did improve, 2.57% to 3.20%, from operating leverage and component in-sourcing - see system-honhai-selfmanufacturing-steelman.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-operating-margin-2025
chunks.text: Hon Hai's consolidated operating margin was 3.20 percent in 2025, up from 2.57 percent in 2018. Hon Hai's March 2026 Enterprise Value Enhancement Plan sets 'operating margin above 3%' as a formal operating indicator, confirmed on the Q1 2026 call by rotating CEO Michael Chiang. That a 3% operating margin is a stated corporate TARGET is itself the answer to whether integration is a high-margin business.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-q1-2026-margins
chunks.text: Hon Hai reported a 6.18 percent gross margin and a 3.57 percent operating margin on 2.12 trillion New Taiwan dollars of revenue in the first quarter of 2026. Two independent T1 records of the same quarter agree exactly. Revenue +29% YoY in NTD, +35% in USD. Value field carries the operating margin.

chunks.heading: system-honhai-selfmanufacturing-steelman
chunks.text: Hon Hai said it is expanding into liquid cooling, mechanical components, high-speed transmission, power modules and system validation to raise its self-manufacturing ratio of key components. THE STEELMAN for integration as a real business, named and attributed. Chiang's argument: pure assembly is a pass-through, so the escape route is owning the differentiated components. The evidence that it works is elsewhere in this layer - Asia Vital Components' operating margin went 2.47% to 19.73% doing exactly this, and Delta's 7.66% to 15.13%. The evidence it is not automatic is Inventec, stuck at 1.84%. Hon Hai's own operating margin rose 2.57% to 3.20% over eight years.

chunks.heading: system-hpe-server-gross-margin-fy2025
chunks.text: HPE's Server segment gross margin fell to 20.9 percent in fiscal 2025 from 29.4 percent in fiscal 2023. FY2023 figure derived from the same filing's segment table (14,266 minus 10,071 over 14,266 = 29.4%); the 20.9% for FY2025 is stated by HPE. FY2024 was 25.1%. HPE attributes group revenue growth to 'higher average unit prices in the Server segment' - it is reselling accelerator content.

chunks.heading: system-hpe-server-operating-margin-fy2025
chunks.text: HPE's Server segment operating margin fell to 7.6 percent in fiscal 2025 from 12.7 percent in fiscal 2023, while segment revenue grew 24 percent. Segment operating profit fell from $1,815M (FY2023) to $1,343M (FY2025), a 26% decline, on revenue up from $14,266M to $17,745M. The sharpest single statement of the pass-through thesis at a US OEM. NOTE: HPE merged Server into a new 'Cloud & AI' segment effective 1 November 2025, so FY2025 is the last comparable read - the series cannot be extended.

chunks.heading: system-hpe-server-revenue-fy2025
chunks.text: HPE's Server segment total net revenue was 17,745 million dollars in fiscal 2025. For scale against Dell ISG ($60,826M) and Supermicro ($21,973M) in overlapping fiscal years. HPE discloses no AI-systems revenue figure and stopped disclosing an AI backlog figure in its FY2026 earnings releases.

chunks.heading: system-integration-margin-ladder-2026q1
chunks.text: In the first quarter of 2026 rack integrators reported operating margins of 1.8 to 3.6 percent while the thermal, power and connector suppliers into the same racks reported 17.8 to 25.4 percent. The layer's whole answer in one comparison, all from filed statements in a single quarter. Integrators: Inventec 1.80%, Quanta 2.85%, Wistron 3.44%, Hon Hai 3.57%, Wiwynn 6.31%. Suppliers of differentiated rack content: Delta 17.83%, Asia Vital Components 24.51%, Amphenol 25.4% (FY2025), Vertiv 17.9% (FY2025). value nulled deliberately - the claim is a spread, not a point; value_range carries the integrator floor and the supplier ceiling. CAVEAT: company-level margins, mixed end markets, and an undisclosed buy-and-sell vs consignment mix.

chunks.heading: system-integrator-gross-profit-per-rack-estimate
chunks.text: At Quanta's filed first-quarter 2026 margins an integrator retains roughly 143 thousand dollars of gross profit and 86 thousand dollars of operating profit on a 3 million dollar rack. DERIVED ESTIMATE, method stated: Quanta's filed Q1 2026 company-level gross margin (4.78%) and operating margin (2.85%) applied to an assumed $3M rack ASP. Units are dollars, not thousands. At the Morgan Stanley $7.8M Vera Rubin figure the same margins give roughly $373k gross / $222k operating. NOT a rack-specific margin: Quanta's company margin blends notebooks and general servers, and the buy-and-sell versus consignment mix is undisclosed. Order of magnitude only, and the honest way to state the value split - low single-digit percent to the integrator against an accelerator NVIDIA sells at roughly 70%+ gross margin. Do not present as a measured figure.

chunks.heading: system-inventec-operating-margin-2025
chunks.text: Inventec's operating margin was 1.84 percent in 2025, versus 1.48 percent in 2018. The control case. Inventec rode the same AI wave (June 2026 revenue +61.6% YoY) and captured almost none of it: gross margin 4.71% to 5.31% and operating margin 1.48% to 1.84% over seven years. Q1 2026 operating margin 1.80%. Component in-sourcing is not automatic - it is a strategy some of these firms executed and others did not.

chunks.heading: system-nvidia-us-500bn-plan
chunks.text: NVIDIA said it plans to produce up to 500 billion dollars of AI infrastructure in the United States with named partners. Company plan with no stated time horizon in the cited post, no contractual basis and no breakdown by partner or site - a plan, not announced, booked, shipped or recognised. Must carry forecast treatment. The concrete facilities actually named in the same post total a few hundred thousand square feet and a few hundred million dollars of commitment, which is the gap worth showing.

chunks.heading: system-nvl72-coolant-flow-2lps
chunks.text: The NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 rack circulates coolant at 2 litres per second, entering at 25 degrees Celsius and leaving at 45 degrees. NEW UNIT TOKEN 'L_per_s' introduced by this pass - no prior corpus entry uses it; confirm at merge. The 20C rise across 120 kW is the specification that created the CDU, manifold and cold-plate market where Vertiv and Asia Vital Components earn 18-25% operating margins.

chunks.heading: system-nvl72-copper-spine-length
chunks.text: The NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 NVLink spine contains more than 2 miles of copper cabling. Roughly 5,000 cables (SemiAnalysis states 5,184 direct-drive, 288 per NVSwitch). This is the physical reason a connector and cable-assembly firm - Amphenol at 25.4% operating margin - captures more of a rack than the company that bolts it together. SemiAnalysis source is partially paywalled; the cited figures are in the free portion.

chunks.heading: system-nvl72-copper-vs-optics-20kw
chunks.text: Using copper rather than optical transceivers in the GB200 NVL72 spine saves 20 kilowatts per rack. One sixth of the rack's entire 120 kW budget, attributed to Jensen Huang (NVIDIA CEO) at GTC 2024. The design decision that made rack-scale a copper-and-mechanical problem rather than an optics problem, and correspondingly shifted supplier value.

chunks.heading: system-nvl72-rack-power-120kw
chunks.text: The NVIDIA DGX GB200 NVL72 rack draws 120 kilowatts. Roughly 10x a conventional air-cooled enterprise rack. The number that forced liquid cooling, busbars and power shelves into the product and moved profit to the suppliers of those parts. Hands-on trade-press reporting from GTC 2024; NVIDIA's own product pages state 'fully liquid-cooled' without a kW figure.

chunks.heading: system-nvl72-rack-weight-1360kg
chunks.text: The NVIDIA DGX GB200 NVL72 rack weighs 1.36 metric tonnes. 3,000 lb. Determines floor loading, freight, rigging and why final integration increasingly happens near the datacenter rather than only in Asia. Composed of 18 compute trays and 9 NVLink switch trays.

chunks.heading: system-quanta-gross-margin-round-trip
chunks.text: Quanta's gross margin was 4.78 percent in the first quarter of 2026, the same level as full-year 2019, after peaking at 7.85 percent in 2024. The single most important number in this layer and, as far as this pass could establish, unreported. Quanta's AI margin expansion is a completed round trip: 4.78% (2019) to 7.85% (2024) to 6.98% (2025) to 4.78% (Q1 2026) - and the Q1 2026 reading came in the quarter its revenue grew 103% YoY. The GB200/GB300 full-rack mix is more dilutive than the HGX-board mix it replaced. Operating margin 2.85% in Q1 2026 vs 4.37% in 2024. CAVEAT: company-level, not rack-specific, and the buy-and-sell vs consignment mix is undisclosed (see system-honhai-consignment-model-asic).

chunks.heading: system-quanta-revenue-2025
chunks.text: Quanta's consolidated revenue was 2,124 billion New Taiwan dollars in 2025, up 51 percent from 1,411 billion in 2024. Roughly US$68bn. Quanta more than doubled revenue versus 2019 (NT$1,030bn) while ending Q1 2026 on the same gross margin.

chunks.heading: system-smci-cash-drawdown-2026q3
chunks.text: Super Micro Computer's cash and cash equivalents fell from 5.2 billion dollars at June 30 2025 to 1.3 billion dollars at March 31 2026. The filing names the causes: inventory build for future revenue, 'greater requests for longer payment terms from customers due to increasing system costs' and 'longer supply chain lead times on certain key components'. Evidence that working capital, not factory floor space, is the binding constraint on doubling rack output.

chunks.heading: system-smci-customer-concentration-2026q3
chunks.text: Four customers accounted for 75.1 percent of Super Micro Computer's accounts receivable at March 31 2026, the largest at 32.2 percent. Sum of the four disclosed customers (32.2+16.8+13.2+12.9). A year earlier only two customers exceeded 10%. Concentration risk compounds with a 6-10% gross margin and a shrinking cash balance: see system-smci-cash-drawdown.

chunks.heading: system-smci-gm-9m-fy2026
chunks.text: Super Micro Computer's gross margin for the nine months ended March 31 2026 was 8.2 percent, down from 11.6 percent a year earlier. Company's own table states the 3.4-point decline. Same filing attributes the cost increase to 'GPU servers, HPC systems, and rack-scale solutions'. Q3 alone was 9.9%.

chunks.heading: system-smci-gm-fy2023
chunks.text: Super Micro Computer reported an 18.0 percent gross margin on 7.12 billion dollars of revenue in fiscal 2023. Pre-AI-mix peak. Computed as gross profit divided by net sales from the filed statements; the same numbers are in SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0001375365). This is the top of the series that every later Supermicro margin should be read against.

chunks.heading: system-smci-gm-fy2025
chunks.text: Super Micro Computer reported an 11.1 percent gross margin on 21.97 billion dollars of revenue in fiscal 2025. Revenue tripled versus FY2023 while gross margin fell 6.9 percentage points. Operating margin over the same span: 10.7% (FY2023) to 5.7% (FY2025).

chunks.heading: system-smci-gm-q2fy2026
chunks.text: Super Micro Computer reported a 6.3 percent gross margin on 12.68 billion dollars of net sales in the quarter ended December 31 2025. Lowest gross margin in Supermicro's public history, recorded in its largest revenue quarter ever (revenue roughly 2.2x the year-ago quarter). Derived from filed gross profit of $0.80bn over $12.68bn of net sales via SEC XBRL; the 10-Q carries both line items.

chunks.heading: system-smci-om-fy2025
chunks.text: Super Micro Computer's operating margin fell from 10.7 percent in fiscal 2023 to 5.7 percent in fiscal 2025. Operating income grew only 65% (from $761M to $1,253M) while revenue grew 209%. Derived from filed operating income over net sales.

chunks.heading: system-smci-tariff-expense-2026q3
chunks.text: Super Micro Computer's tariff expense rose 89.4 million dollars, or 608 percent year over year, in the quarter ended March 31 2026. Against $1,019M of gross profit in the same quarter, i.e. roughly 8.8% of gross profit. The systems layer is where trade policy first becomes a P&L line item.

chunks.heading: system-tw-odm-h1-2026-revenue-growth
chunks.text: Quanta's and Wistron's cumulative revenue for the first half of 2026 rose 86.5 percent and 94.0 percent year over year respectively. Exchange-filed monthly revenue. Hon Hai's own filing note for June 2026 states the cause in Chinese: mainly benefiting from increased server shipments. Wistron's: mainly customer demand increased. Value carries the Wistron figure. Hon Hai June 2026 alone: NT$821.8bn, +52.1% YoY.

chunks.heading: system-vertiv-operating-margin-expansion
chunks.text: Vertiv's operating margin rose from 4.9 percent in 2020 to 17.9 percent in 2025, on revenue up from 4.37 to 10.23 billion dollars. The US-listed thermal-and-power counterpart to Asia Vital Components and Delta: coolant distribution units, sidecars, busway, UPS. Margin roughly 5x an ODM's on the infrastructure that liquid-cooled rack-scale requires. Derived from filed revenue and operating income; the underlying line items are in Vertiv's 10-K for FY2025.

chunks.heading: system-vr200-nvl72-rack-price-estimate
chunks.text: Morgan Stanley estimated the NVIDIA Vera Rubin VR200 NVL72 rack at about 7.8 million dollars bought from an ODM, assuming NVIDIA resells procured content at a 70 percent gross margin. ESTIMATE, not a price. Whose: Morgan Stanley (Howard Kao). The 70% assumed NVIDIA gross margin on resold content is the analyst's assumption, not a disclosure. Same note: about $6.7M if the hyperscaler buys memory modules directly. LOW confidence for two reasons - the primary note is not accessible, and it reaches us only through aggregators. Tom's Hardware separately reports up to $8.8M, which appears to be the higher-end NVL144 VR300 rather than VR200; the $7.0-8.8M spread is unreconciled. If this number is used on the site it must be labelled as a Morgan Stanley estimate with the range shown.

chunks.heading: system-wistron-doubled-revenue-lower-margin-2025
chunks.text: Wistron's revenue grew 108 percent to 2,187 billion New Taiwan dollars in 2025 while its gross margin fell from 8.01 to 6.13 percent. A textbook pass-through signature: revenue slightly more than doubled, gross margin fell 1.9 points, and operating margin barely moved (3.71% to 3.59%). The incremental dollar arrived carrying its own cost. Q1 2026: gross margin 5.21%, operating margin 3.44% on NT$846.3bn of revenue.

chunks.heading: system-wistron-fort-worth-plant
chunks.text: Wistron opened a 324,000 square foot AI systems factory in Fort Worth, Texas on July 21 2026 under a roughly 700 million dollar commitment. NEW UNIT TOKEN 'sqft' introduced by this pass (corpus has M_sqft only); confirm at merge. First GB300 compute baseboard built in the United States. Named 'D1'. DigiTimes article is paywalled beyond the preview; the cited figures are in the free portion and match NVIDIA's own post. Scale check: 324,000 sq ft against Foxconn's stated >1 million sq ft of planned US AI-server space and Hon Hai's >40 US facilities.

chunks.heading: system-wiwynn-margin-premium-2025
chunks.text: Wiwynn earned a 6.72 percent operating margin in 2025 against Quanta's 4.12 percent, on one-fifth of Quanta's revenue. Wiwynn sells rack-scale systems directly to hyperscalers rather than through NVIDIA's OEM channel, and consistently earns roughly 1.6-2x the operating margin of the merchant ODMs. Its margin is ALSO compressing on AI volume (10.37% to 8.25% gross as revenue grew 163%), so the channel premium does not exempt it from mix dilution. Q1 2026: 7.55% gross, 6.31% operating.

chunks.heading: The verdict
chunks.text:
Verdict for the agent-infra layer: overbuilt. Frontier labs now price this layer's primitives at or near zero, and one of them has switched off its own orchestrator. The capital here is priced against work that keeps moving into the model API.

The counter, per Temporal's own Series C disclosures, March 2025 — company-reported and unaudited: Durable execution is not a model capability. Temporal reports 184% net dollar retention and more than 2,500 cloud customers on retries, timers and crash-surviving state — a better model does not make a workflow idempotent.

chunks.heading: Introduction
chunks.text:
agent-infra — Introduction. Every bear case for this layer says the model will eat it. The evidence says something narrower and more useful: what gets absorbed is token-marshalling — routing, retrieval, sandboxing, prompt plumbing — and what survives is anything that makes a guarantee about state.

The sharpest datapoint is not a startup death. OpenAI announced Agent Builder, a visual canvas for multi-step agent workflows, in October 2025, and has scheduled it for shutdown on 30 November 2026 . A frontier lab shipped a first-party competitor to the orchestration products in this layer and switched it off inside a year. There are two honest readings and this page carries both.

chunks.heading: What this layer is
chunks.text:
agent-infra — What this layer is. The plumbing between a model API and something that runs in production: orchestration, retrieval, sandboxing, evals and observability, plus the connector standard tying tools to models.

That last piece is the only part with a countable population, so it serves as the anchor. The Model Context Protocol had more than 10,000 active public servers and more than 97 million monthly SDK downloads as of December 2025 — Anthropic's own count, corroborated on a property Anthropic controls, with client support in ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot and VS Code. Adoption by direct competitors is the durable part. Then Anthropic gave the spec away: MCP became a founding project of the Agentic AI Foundation, a Linux Foundation directed fund co-founded with Block and OpenAI, in December 2025 . Owning the connector standard is no longer available as a moat, which removes a risk and a differentiator at once.

chunks.heading: Unit economics
chunks.text:
agent-infra — Unit economics. Almost everything here meters a derivative of token throughput one layer down. Orchestration bills on agent steps: Temporal Cloud's entry plan is $100 a month including one million Actions, with marginal Actions from $50 down to $25 per million at volume . Observability bills on traces under four different names — Arize AX Pro at $50 a month for 50,000 spans , Braintrust Pro at $249 for 50,000 scores , Langfuse at $8 per 100,000 units of overage graduating to $6 above 50 million , and Weights & Biases at $0.10 per megabyte of Weave ingestion above a 1.5 gigabyte allowance . Retrieval bills on storage and reads: Pinecone at a $50 monthly minimum, $16–18 per million read units and $0.33 per gigabyte per month , with Chroma at an identical $0.33 headline . Where the product is a user interface it bills on seats — LangSmith Plus at $39 per seat per month .

Two vendors price in units designed to defeat comparison: turbopuffer publishes monthly minimums of $16, $256 and $4,096, the top tier carrying a 35% usage premium, and no per-unit rate at all , while LlamaCloud sells credits at $1.25 per thousand . Opacity is a pricing strategy in this sub-segment, and worth naming rather than modelling around.

chunks.heading: Unit economics
chunks.text:
Two vendors price in units designed to defeat comparison: turbopuffer publishes monthly minimums of $16, $256 and $4,096, the top tier carrying a 35% usage premium, and no per-unit rate at all , while LlamaCloud sells credits at $1.25 per thousand . Opacity is a pricing strategy in this sub-segment, and worth naming rather than modelling around.

Now the price they compete against. Gemini File Search charges $0.15 per million tokens to index once, and nothing for storage or query-time embedding generation . Pinecone's entire meter is what Google gives away. Sandboxes are the same story: Anthropic grants 1,550 free container-hours per organization per month, then $0.05 per container-hour, and charges nothing when code execution runs alongside web search or web fetch — the most common agent pattern there is ; OpenAI charges $0.03 for a 20-minute 1 GB session rising to $1.92 at 64 GB . Against that, E2B Pro is $150 a month plus usage , Daytona bills $0.0858 per vCPU-hour , and Modal charges a threefold markup over its own standard compute rate for the sandbox wrapper around the same silicon . Cloudflare's move is bundling rather than price: 25 GiB-hours of container memory and 375 vCPU-minutes arrive inside a Workers plan the customer already pays for .

What the corpus does not have, and this page will not fabricate: no framework revenue. Not LangChain, not LlamaIndex, not CrewAI. Zero disclosed revenue figures for the sub-segment that gets the most attention.

chunks.heading: The players
chunks.text:
agent-infra — The players. Orchestration. Temporal is the strongest survival case in the layer and it is not an AI company. It raised $146m at a $1.72bn post-money valuation in March 2025 , disclosing 184% net dollar retention, more than 2,500 Cloud customers and 4.4 times revenue growth over the preceding 18 months — company-selected metrics in a funding announcement, unaudited. Note what they are claims about: durable execution is an operational guarantee, not a model capability. LangChain, by contrast, was valued at $1.25bn in an October 2025 Series B of $125m led by IVP , with no company-disclosed revenue figure in the corpus to set against it. CrewAI publishes no list price above a free tier capped at 50 workflow executions a month, and quotes its enterprise plan in 50 hours of development per month — at the top tier the monetized unit is services time, not software.

Evals and observability. Braintrust raised $80m led by ICONIQ at a reported $800m valuation in February 2026, on $121m raised in total — the valuation appears in press coverage rather than the company's own post, hence medium confidence. It discloses no ARR, customer count or volume metric anywhere, so no multiple can be computed, and this page says so instead of estimating one. Arize raised a $70m Series C with M12, Datadog and PagerDuty participating : the two APM incumbents most exposed to AI observability bought an option rather than building. And the category's biggest name left — CoreWeave completed its acquisition of Weights & Biases, with roughly a million users, in May 2025 in a transaction reported at $1.7bn .

The competitive set Ashutosh named is the substance — AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle and Databricks, platforms that added vector search as a feature — and he said acquisition is not on the table, which is the on-record answer to every claim that Pinecone is for sale. On revenue there is one number and it is weak: Latka estimates $26.6m of ARR for 2025, unchanged from 2024, against a $750m valuation that is the April 2023 mark . Latka is a modelled, self-reported database; naming that is better than repeating the figure anonymously, which is what most commentary here does.

chunks.heading: Concentration & chokepoints
chunks.text:
agent-infra — Concentration & chokepoints. The chokepoint is a price list, not a supply chain. Three vendors set the marginal cost of every primitive in this layer, and a sandbox session from them runs between three cents and free . A standalone vendor's floor is somebody else's rounding error.

The second chokepoint is measurement. The 10,000-server figure is Anthropic's own count corroborated on Anthropic's own property , and third-party registry counts diverge by an order of magnitude — every source for them was an inadmissible aggregator. A layer nobody can count is a layer nobody can size, including the people raising against it.

chunks.heading: Lead times & capacity
chunks.text: agent-infra — Lead times & capacity. There is no queue here, and pretending otherwise would be the easiest dishonest paragraph on this site. Capacity is a line in a pricing table: E2B Pro allows up to 100 concurrent sandboxes and 24-hour sessions ; Cloudflare's included allowance is 375 vCPU-minutes a month . What doubles when demand doubles is the bill — and because the meters are derivatives of step count and trace volume , that is why revenue in this layer can grow while its pricing power does not.

chunks.heading: 2019 → today
chunks.text:
agent-infra — 2019 → today. The corpus has no pre-2025 anchor here, so the three-snapshot treatment used elsewhere on this site does not apply. What it has instead is an absorption timeline compressed into about a year.

November 2025. Anthropic's code-execution-with-MCP example cut agent token consumption from 150,000 to 2,000, a 98.7% reduction ; three weeks later its Tool Search Tool cut token usage 85% and Programmatic Tool Calling took a complex research task from 43,588 to 27,297 tokens . Both are company-published benchmarks, not independent replication. In between, Google launched File Search with free storage and free query-time embeddings .

December 2025 to now. MCP governance leaves Anthropic for the Agentic AI Foundation , Anthropic makes code execution free when bundled with web search , Google cuts grounded search from $35 to $14 per thousand queries in one model generation , and OpenAI schedules its own orchestrator for shutdown . Every one of those events lowers what a third party can charge.

chunks.heading: Commoditization pressure
chunks.text:
agent-infra — Commoditization pressure. Here is the counterintuitive part, and it runs against how this layer is usually argued. Evals and observability is the least durable sub-segment, not the most. The durability case is that as models improve the bottleneck moves to knowing whether your system works, which is customer-specific and therefore unabsorbable. Demand, granted. Pricing power, no: four vendors meter near-identical units within roughly one order of magnitude , one of them is open-source-core and therefore sets the ceiling for the rest , and the category's most valuable asset ended up as a differentiator on a GPU cloud's bill . Note the direction of that last one: absorption from below, by the compute vendor, not from above by the model — a different failure mode than the one the bear case names.

Retrieval is deflating fastest, and inside the API rather than against it: grounded search went from $35 to $14 per thousand queries in one model generation . No standalone vendor's cost base moves at that rate.

The exception has a shape, and it is not an AI-native one. Temporal's claim is about retries, timers and state that survives a crash . A better model does not make a workflow idempotent. The durable businesses in this layer are the ones that would have existed without LLMs.

chunks.heading: Failure modes
chunks.text:
agent-infra — Failure modes. Absorption of the marshalling layer. Tool routing, tool registries and prompt plumbing were products; within three weeks in November 2025 two of them became features . Blast radius is confined to vendors whose value-add sits between the model and its tools.

Bundling, which is quieter than absorption and works better. Sandboxing arrives inside a Workers plan already being paid for and free alongside a search call . Nobody has to win on product to win here.

Revenue coupled to upstream prices. Because the meters are derivatives of token and step volume , a price cut one layer down is a revenue cut in this one .

Valuation without a denominator. Braintrust at a reported $800m discloses no revenue metric ; LangChain at $1.25bn discloses none either . When three companies are setting the layer's marginal price toward zero, an unpriceable private mark is the fragility rather than the funding.

chunks.heading: Open questions
chunks.text: agent-infra — Open questions. - Is Agent Builder's shutdown a verdict on orchestration, or on model-locked orchestration? The bear reading is that the lab concluded the model handles decomposition. The steelman is that a first-party tool tied to one model family is simply a worse product than a neutral one — and Temporal's retention is the evidence for it . - What is anyone's revenue? The corpus holds no disclosed ARR for a single independent vendor in this layer. Its one figure is a tier-3 model for Pinecone , and nothing should be load-bearing on it. - Does durable execution stay outside the model, and does open-source-core cap everything else? The layer's one non-absorbable thesis rests on unaudited metrics from a single vendor, and Langfuse's published schedule already ceilings closed vendors on traces — whether that dynamic reaches orchestration and retrieval is untested. - Who counts MCP? One organization publishes the number, third-party counts diverge by an order of magnitude, and the body now governing the spec publishes none .

chunks.heading: The verdict
chunks.text:
Verdict for the applications layer: overbuilt. The revenue is real and compounding. The prices are set against denominators one research shop estimates and nobody audits, and the layer's only public margin datapoint crosses zero.

The counter, per The SpaceX–Anysphere deal and Harvey's own March 2026 disclosure: SpaceX paid $60bn in stock for Cursor, and Harvey's own count is 100,000 lawyers at 1,300 organisations. One is an arm's-length transaction, the other a company disclosure. Neither is a mark.

chunks.heading: Introduction
chunks.text:
applications — Introduction. This is where the stack's dollar finally becomes revenue. It is also the layer the site knows least about.

Every layer below this one is measured in filings. Here, almost nothing is. The revenue figures for Harvey, Abridge, Decagon, Replit, Lovable and Clay are estimates published by one research shop — Sacra — and then restated by aggregators that add no measurement of their own. Restatement is not corroboration. So this page names the estimator every time, and where a company has published a figure of its own it wins; where a valuation multiple is printed, the page says which denominator it used.

chunks.heading: What this layer is
chunks.text:
applications — What this layer is. Three businesses wearing one label.

Horizontal assistants sold to everyone. ChatGPT is the layer's only consumer-scale asset: more than 900 million weekly active users on OpenAI's own count as of February 2026, alongside more than 50 million consumer subscribers and more than 9 million paying business users . A separate 1-billion figure for monthly active app users is a Sensor Tower estimate relayed by Reuters, crossed in June 2026 — not an OpenAI disclosure .

Vertical apps sold to one profession. Harvey and Legora to lawyers, Abridge to clinicians, Glean to the enterprise's own documents, Clay to revenue teams.

Agents priced by the outcome. Sierra and Decagon in customer support, and Intercom's Fin, which publishes the cleanest price in the layer: $0.99 per outcome, billed only when it resolves an issue end to end or executes a configured procedure .

The physical anchor is a login and a meter. A lawyer's seat starting near $1,200 a month ; a resolved support ticket at $0.99 . Behind both sits a token bill the vendor does not set.

chunks.heading: Unit economics
chunks.text:
applications — Unit economics. Seat pricing still dominates, and it is priced like enterprise software rather than like a metered utility. Harvey's base offering starts at about $1,200 per lawyer per month on twelve-month commitments — Sacra's wording is "starts at", so treat it as a floor, and note that Harvey publishes no pricing at all. Abridge sits an order of magnitude lower per user: roughly $2,500 per clinician per year , single-sourced, with the bottom-up comparators in the same note also unverified.

Outcome pricing is the genuine innovation, and it is small but real. Fin's $0.99 is a live published price on Intercom's own page, subject to a monthly outcome minimum. It transfers model-cost risk from the buyer to the vendor, which is exactly why the margin question below matters more here than in any software layer before it.

Two margin datapoints exist for the whole layer, and both are weak. OpenAI's gross margin was approximately 33% for FY2025 — an analyst estimate, because OpenAI publishes no audited margin. And Replit's gross margin fluctuated between positive 36% and negative 14% during 2025 , which Sacra attributes to the cost of running its coding agents.

That Replit range is the most load-bearing sentence on this page, so the site will state its fragility plainly: it is a range that crosses zero, which is why the corpus refuses to record a single number for it; it has no independent source at any date, because Replit is private and discloses nothing; and it is one unsourced sentence from one research shop. It is also the only public evidence anywhere that agentic cost of goods can invert an application's margin. Replit's own response — replacing flat checkpoint pricing with effort-based agent pricing — is consistent with the problem being real.

chunks.heading: The players
chunks.text:
applications — The players. Coding is the deepest pocket. Cursor reached $1bn annualized in November 2025 and $3bn by May 2026 , then produced the layer's first mega-exit: an all-stock acquisition by SpaceX valuing Anysphere at $60bn, announced 16 June 2026 . Lovable reached about $500m annualized in mid-2026 with 146 full-time employees in February 2026 . The revenue-per-employee figure in circulation for Lovable mixes a mid-2026 revenue with a February headcount; the site will not print it, because on matched dates it is materially lower. Replit reached about $525m annualized in April 2026 , single-sourced.

The labs are themselves applications. Anthropic disclosed a $14bn run rate on 12 February 2026 and $47bn by May , with roughly 70–75% of revenue from pay-per-token API calls on Sacra's estimate . Do not restate that as "80% from API": the independently corroborated ~80% figure is revenue from business customers, a different cut . Claude Code is reported at $2.5bn annualized in February 2026 — Sacra-only, and flagged in the corpus as unable to anchor a headline claim alone.

Legal is a two-horse capital race. Harvey served more than 100,000 lawyers across 1,300 organizations in over 60 countries as of March 2026 — its own disclosure . Sacra's user count is materially higher, carries no source, and post-dates Harvey's own by two months, so the site uses the company's. Harvey raised at $11bn in March 2026 on an estimated $300m ARR ; Legora raised $550m at $5.55bn . Harvey's last well-sourced revenue figure is the $100m it reached in August 2025, three years after founding .
